title: iLO Login Failure
description: A single failed iLO login attempt (GUI, SSH, Redfish, or REST API). The atomic building block for the brute-force/spray/successful-after-failures detections below. iLO is out-of-band management — it operates independently of the host OS's own power state, so authentication events here are visible even when the managed ProLiant server itself is powered off.

data_sources.name: iLO Security Log
data_sources.description: Login attempt records with source, protocol, and outcome.

detection_logic: Filters the iLO security/event log for authentication failure events across all access protocols.
spl:
index=ilo sourcetype=ilo_security event="Login" result="Failed"
| table _time, host, user, src_ip, interface
tuning_guidance: Expect routine noise; use ILO-002/003 for volume-based detection.
investigation_steps: Confirm src_ip is a known out-of-band management source.
response_guidance: No action for an isolated failure.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Repeated iLO Login Failures / Brute Force
description: Five or more failed iLO login attempts within 10 minutes. Because iLO is Tier-0/Tier-1 out-of-band infrastructure that can bypass the operating system entirely (power, console, firmware, boot, and storage control), this deserves the same low alert threshold as a domain controller or a hypervisor management interface.

data_sources.name: iLO Security Log
data_sources.description: Authentication failures.

detection_logic: Counts failed iLO logins per device in a rolling window.
spl:
index=ilo sourcetype=ilo_security event="Login" result="Failed"
| bin _time span=10m
| stats count, dc(user) as distinct_users, values(src_ip) as source_ips by host, _time
| where count>=5
tuning_guidance: Minimal legitimate tuning expected; out-of-band management interfaces should see a small, predictable volume of authentication traffic.
investigation_steps: Validate targeted usernames.
Check for a subsequent success (ILO-004).
response_guidance: Block the source at the OOB network layer; this interface should never be reachable from a general-purpose network segment in the first place.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: iLO Password Spraying Across Fleet
description: A single source IP attempts authentication against many distinct iLO devices or usernames in a short window — consistent with an attacker who has obtained a candidate password (default credential lists, breach data) and is sweeping the out-of-band management network for any device it works on.

data_sources.name: iLO Security Log (fleet-aggregated)
data_sources.path: iLO Security Log, aggregated across devices
data_sources.description: Authentication failures across the managed fleet.

detection_logic: Counts distinct target devices/usernames attempted per source IP across the fleet in a rolling window.
spl:
index=ilo sourcetype=ilo_security event="Login" result="Failed"
| bin _time span=15m
| stats dc(host) as distinct_devices, dc(user) as distinct_users by src_ip, _time
| where distinct_devices>=5 OR distinct_users>=6
tuning_guidance: Exclude known vulnerability-scanning/asset-discovery source IPs operating on the OOB network under an approved schedule.
investigation_steps: Identify every targeted device.
Check for any success from the source (ILO-004).
response_guidance: Block the source at the OOB network layer immediately; treat as a fleet-wide credential-guessing campaign.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Successful iLO Login Following Repeated Failures
description: A successful iLO login for a user/device pair that had five or more failures in the preceding 30 minutes. Given that iLO compromise grants power, console, firmware, boot, and storage-level control that bypasses the operating system entirely, this ranks among the single highest-priority detections in the entire catalogue.

data_sources.name: iLO Security Log
data_sources.description: Login success/failure sequence.

detection_logic: Joins a failed-login threshold search with a subsequent success for the same user/device within 30 minutes.
spl:
index=ilo sourcetype=ilo_security event="Login"
| eval outcome=if(result="Failed","fail","success")
| transaction user, host maxspan=30m startswith=eval(outcome="fail") endswith=eval(outcome="success")
| where eventcount>=6
| table _time, host, user, src_ip, eventcount
tuning_guidance: Very low expected false-positive rate given how tightly OOB management access should normally be scoped.
investigation_steps: Treat as a live incident.
Immediately check for Virtual Media mounts, boot overrides, firmware changes, and new user creation in the same session (RC-###, VMEDIA-###, FW-###, ILO-010).
response_guidance: Disable the account, disconnect any active session (console/virtual media), and audit every action taken during the session before doing anything else — this session may have already achieved boot-level persistence.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: iLO Login From First-Seen Source IP
description: A successful iLO login from a source IP never seen for that device in the prior 30 days. OOB management networks typically have a small, static set of legitimate administrative sources (jump hosts, a dedicated management VLAN), making first-seen events unusually high-signal compared to general IT infrastructure.

data_sources.name: iLO Security Log
data_sources.description: Login success events with source IP.

detection_logic: Builds a 30-day baseline of source IPs per device and flags first-seen values.
spl:
index=ilo sourcetype=ilo_security event="Login" result="Success"
| lookup ilo_source_baseline.csv host src_ip OUTPUT is_known
| where isnull(is_known)
| table _time, host, user, src_ip
tuning_guidance: Maintain ilo_source_baseline.csv via a nightly scheduled search rather than an inline subsearch, given the value of this signal on Tier-0 infrastructure.
investigation_steps: Confirm with the administrator directly.
Verify the source is on the designated OOB management network at all.
response_guidance: Suspend the session pending confirmation if unexpected; any source outside the OOB management network warrants immediate escalation regardless of credential validity.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: iLO Login Outside the Out-of-Band Management Network
description: A successful iLO login whose source IP falls outside the CIDR range(s) of the designated out-of-band management network. iLO (like the shared-NIC configuration it can be set to) should in a properly-segmented environment never be reachable from general-purpose production/user networks — a login from outside the OOB range is a strong signal that segmentation has failed or was never correctly implemented.

data_sources.name: iLO Security Log
data_sources.description: Login events with source IP.

detection_logic: Compares login source IP against a maintained lookup of approved OOB management CIDR ranges.
spl:
index=ilo sourcetype=ilo_security event="Login" result="Success"
| lookup ilo_oob_cidrs.csv src_ip OUTPUT is_oob_range
| where isnull(is_oob_range)
| table _time, host, user, src_ip
tuning_guidance: Maintain the OOB CIDR allowlist; review whenever new management jump hosts or VPN pools are added.
investigation_steps: Confirm whether the iLO's NIC is in dedicated or shared mode (ILO-041) — shared mode is far more likely to expose it to a general network.
response_guidance: Treat as Critical: this indicates either a network segmentation failure or unauthorized access, and both require immediate remediation.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: iLO Default Credential Login Attempt
description: A login attempt (successful or failed) using iLO's factory-random-default Administrator account without evidence the default password was ever rotated. Newer iLO generations ship with a unique random default password printed on the pull tab rather than a static one, but fleets provisioned via scripted/unattended workflows sometimes standardize that initial credential across many hosts — a successful login here means the device may never have been individually hardened after deployment.

data_sources.name: iLO Security Log
data_sources.description: Login attempts using the default/pull-tab Administrator account.

detection_logic: Filters login events for the default Administrator username, cross-referenced against a lookup tracking which devices have confirmed post-provisioning credential rotation.
spl:
index=ilo sourcetype=ilo_security event="Login" user="Administrator"
| lookup ilo_default_creds_flag.csv host OUTPUT still_default
| table _time, host, user, src_ip, result, still_default
tuning_guidance: If `still_default` is unknown, treat every successful login on this account as an emergency until you have positively confirmed the pull-tab password was rotated during provisioning.
investigation_steps: Confirm whether the default/pull-tab password was actually changed for this device.
If the login succeeded and the password was still default, treat as a confirmed exposure.
response_guidance: Rotate the credential immediately regardless of outcome and audit the device for any changes made during a successful session.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: iLO SSH or REST API Authentication
description: An administrative session is authenticated via SSH or the legacy REST API rather than the HTTPS GUI or Redfish API. Tracked separately since CLI/API sessions run raw commands that are individually less visible than GUI-driven actions in structured logs.

data_sources.name: iLO Security Log
data_sources.description: Login events by interface/protocol.

detection_logic: Filters login events for the SSH/REST interface.
spl:
index=ilo sourcetype=ilo_security event="Login" result="Success" interface IN ("SSH","REST")
| table _time, host, user, src_ip, interface
tuning_guidance: Baseline expected automation source IPs (deployment tooling, HPE OneView) separately from interactive administrators.
investigation_steps: Cross-reference src_ip against the automation/jump-host allowlist.
response_guidance: No automatic action for expected sources; investigate per ILO-006 if outside the OOB network.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: iLO Session From Dormant or Service Account
description: A successful iLO login using an account that has not authenticated in 90+ days, or a service/automation account (normally used only for API-driven, non-interactive access) authenticating interactively via the GUI or Remote Console.

data_sources.name: iLO Security Log
data_sources.description: Login events cross-referenced against last-seen and account-type lookups.

detection_logic: Joins login success against a last-authenticated-date lookup and an account-type (interactive vs. service) lookup.
spl:
index=ilo sourcetype=ilo_security event="Login" result="Success"
| lookup ilo_last_seen.csv host user OUTPUT last_seen
| lookup ilo_account_type.csv user OUTPUT account_type
| eval days_dormant=round((now()-strptime(last_seen,"%Y-%m-%d"))/86400,0)
| where days_dormant>=90 OR (account_type="service" AND interface="GUI")
| table _time, host, user, src_ip, days_dormant, account_type
tuning_guidance: Requires a maintained last-seen lookup, ideally refreshed nightly.
investigation_steps: Confirm the account owner initiated this session.
For a service account used interactively, verify whether its credential may have been extracted and reused by a human operator.
response_guidance: Disable dormant accounts that should have been offboarded; investigate service-account interactive use as a likely credential-theft indicator.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: New iLO User Created
description: A new local iLO user account is created. Legitimate during provisioning, but also the most direct persistence mechanism available to an attacker who has gained administrative access to out-of-band management infrastructure.

data_sources.name: iLO Security Log
data_sources.description: User account creation events.

detection_logic: Filters the iLO security log for user-creation events.
spl:
index=ilo sourcetype=ilo_security event="UserAdded"
| table _time, host, user, acting_user
tuning_guidance: Correlate with change-management tickets or HPE OneView-driven provisioning workflows.
investigation_steps: Verify against an approved-accounts list.
Check the privilege level assigned (ILO-011).
response_guidance: Disable/delete immediately if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: iLO User Granted Administrator Privilege
description: A user account (new or existing) is granted full Administrator privilege, iLO's highest role, capable of every action this catalogue covers — power control, Virtual Media, firmware, boot configuration, and further account management.

data_sources.name: iLO Security Log
data_sources.description: User privilege-level change events.

detection_logic: Filters the iLO security log for privilege changes granting the Administer User Accounts / full-Administrator privilege bundle.
spl:
index=ilo sourcetype=ilo_security event="UserPrivilegeChanged" privilege="Administrator"
| table _time, host, user, acting_user
tuning_guidance: No routine tuning — every occurrence should map to a change record.
investigation_steps: Verify against change management.
Review what the account does immediately afterward.
response_guidance: Downgrade immediately if unauthorized; treat as a Critical management-plane-compromise indicator.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: iLO User Deleted or Disabled
description: An account is deleted or disabled. Can be routine offboarding, or an attacker removing legitimate administrators' access to hinder incident response after establishing their own persistence account.

data_sources.name: iLO Security Log
data_sources.description: User deletion/disable events.

detection_logic: Filters the iLO security log for user deletion/disable events.
spl:
index=ilo sourcetype=ilo_security (event="UserDeleted" OR event="UserDisabled")
| table _time, host, user, acting_user
tuning_guidance: Correlate with offboarding workflows for routine cases.
investigation_steps: Confirm against offboarding records.
Check for a corresponding new-account-creation event around the same time (account swap pattern).
response_guidance: Investigate if unaccounted for, particularly if it removes a legitimate security-team account.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1531: Account Access Removal

author: Threat Detection Library

title: iLO Account Lockout Policy or Password Policy Weakened
description: The account lockout threshold/duration, minimum password complexity, or session-idle timeout policy is weakened. Directly enables the brute-force/spray scenarios detected elsewhere in this catalogue (ILO-002/003) to succeed with less resistance.

data_sources.name: iLO Security Log
data_sources.description: Authentication policy configuration changes.

detection_logic: Filters the iLO security log for authentication-policy configuration changes.
spl:
index=ilo sourcetype=ilo_security event="ConfigChange" cfgattr IN ("AuthFailureLogging","AuthFailuresBeforeDelay","PasswordComplexity","SessionTimeout")
| table _time, host, acting_user, cfgattr
tuning_guidance: Legitimate for a documented troubleshooting scenario — require a change ticket and time-box any weakening.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification.
Check for a subsequent brute-force/spray attempt (ILO-002/003).
response_guidance: Revert to organizational standard immediately.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1556.004: Network Device Authentication

author: Threat Detection Library

title: iLO Directory Service (AD/LDAP) Authentication Changed
description: The Active Directory/LDAP configuration used for centralized iLO authentication is modified — server address, bind credentials, or role-group mapping (HPE iLO's Directory Groups feature). An attacker who controls this configuration can point authentication at a rogue directory server, or broaden a directory-group mapping to grant iLO Administrator privilege to a group they already control.

data_sources.name: iLO Security Log
data_sources.description: Directory service configuration changes.

detection_logic: Filters the iLO security log for AD/LDAP configuration changes.
spl:
index=ilo sourcetype=ilo_security event="ConfigChange" cfgattr IN ("DirectoryServerAddress","DirectoryGroupMapping","LdapBindDN")
| table _time, host, acting_user, cfgattr
tuning_guidance: Legitimate during planned identity-infrastructure migrations; require a change ticket, especially for directory-group mapping changes.
investigation_steps: Verify the new server/group against known-good directory infrastructure.
Audit all logins relying on this trust since the change.
response_guidance: Revert unauthorized changes immediately.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1556.004: Network Device Authentication

author: Threat Detection Library

title: New Directory Group Granted iLO Administrator Access
description: A new Active Directory/LDAP group is mapped to iLO's Administrator role. Since group membership is managed entirely outside iLO (in the directory itself), this single mapping change means anyone an attacker later adds to that AD group — with no further iLO-side action or visibility — gains full iLO Administrator access.

data_sources.name: iLO Security Log
data_sources.description: Directory group role-mapping changes.

detection_logic: Filters the iLO security log for directory-group-to-role mapping changes granting Administrator.
spl:
index=ilo sourcetype=ilo_security event="DirectoryGroupMapped" role="Administrator"
| table _time, host, acting_user, group_name
tuning_guidance: No routine tuning — correlate against change management and confirm the mapped group is a known, tightly-governed privileged-access group.
investigation_steps: Identify the AD/LDAP group and its current membership.
Cross-reference against directory-side privileged-group-change alerting if available.
response_guidance: Remove the mapping immediately if unauthorized; audit AD group membership for the mapped group.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: iLO Local Authentication Fallback Enabled Over Directory
description: Local-account fallback authentication is enabled on a device where centralized AD/LDAP authentication is the expected mechanism, or the fallback broadens beyond a declared break-glass account. Bypasses centralized MFA and identity-governance controls in favor of locally-managed, often weaker-governed credentials.

data_sources.name: iLO Security Log
data_sources.description: Local-authentication fallback configuration changes.

detection_logic: Filters the iLO security log for local-authentication-fallback enablement.
spl:
index=ilo sourcetype=ilo_security event="ConfigChange" cfgattr="LocalAuthFallback" cfgattr_value="Enabled"
| table _time, host, acting_user
tuning_guidance: A single declared break-glass account with local fallback is normal; broadening beyond that is not.
investigation_steps: Confirm this matches the declared break-glass procedure.
response_guidance: Restrict fallback to the single documented break-glass account if broadened.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1556: Modify Authentication Process

author: Threat Detection Library

title: iLO Remote Console Session Started
description: An iLO Remote Console (Integrated Remote Console / .NET / HTML5) session is started, giving the operator interactive keyboard/video/mouse access to the managed server as if physically present at the console — including access to BIOS/RBSU setup, boot menus, and any unlocked OS session, entirely bypassing normal network-based access controls on the host. This is one of the highest-value capabilities iLO exposes and the baseline detection for the higher-priority console detections below.

data_sources.name: iLO Security Log
data_sources.description: Remote Console session start/end events.

detection_logic: Filters the iLO security log for Remote Console session-start events.
spl:
index=ilo sourcetype=ilo_security event="RemoteConsoleSessionStart"
| table _time, host, user, src_ip
tuning_guidance: Baseline expected administrator source IPs and typical session frequency per device; console access should be infrequent on most production servers outside maintenance windows.
investigation_steps: Confirm the session against a change ticket or known maintenance activity.
Check session duration and any subsequent BIOS/boot/media changes (RC-004 through RC-006).
response_guidance: No automatic action for expected sessions; escalate per the more specific console detections below for anomalous ones.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: iLO Remote Console Session From Unusual Source or Outside Maintenance Window
description: A Remote Console session originates from a source IP not on the known-administrator baseline, or starts outside a declared maintenance window. Given the console's ability to bypass every OS-level control, an unexplained session here deserves elevated scrutiny even without any further suspicious activity.

data_sources.name: iLO Security Log
data_sources.description: Console session events cross-referenced against a source baseline and maintenance-window lookup.

detection_logic: Joins console session-start events against a source-IP baseline and a maintenance-window lookup.
spl:
index=ilo sourcetype=ilo_security event="RemoteConsoleSessionStart"
| lookup ilo_source_baseline.csv host src_ip OUTPUT is_known
| lookup ilo_maintenance_windows.csv host _time OUTPUT in_window
| where isnull(is_known) OR isnull(in_window)
| table _time, host, user, src_ip
tuning_guidance: Maintain both lookups; without them this degrades to a high-volume, low-precision alert.
investigation_steps: Confirm against change management.
Review the full session for BIOS/boot/media changes.
response_guidance: Terminate the session and investigate if unconfirmed.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Multiple Concurrent iLO Remote Console Sessions
description: More than one Remote Console session is active on the same device simultaneously — unusual for routine single-operator maintenance and potentially indicating either a shared/compromised credential being used by two parties at once, or an attacker's session running alongside a legitimate administrator's.

data_sources.name: iLO Security Log
data_sources.description: Overlapping console session start/end events per device.

detection_logic: Identifies overlapping session-start/end intervals for the same device.
spl:
index=ilo sourcetype=ilo_security (event="RemoteConsoleSessionStart" OR event="RemoteConsoleSessionEnd")
| transaction host maxevents=2 startswith=eval(event="RemoteConsoleSessionStart")
| where mvcount(user)>1
| table _time, host, user, src_ip
tuning_guidance: Some organizations legitimately allow shared/collaborative console sessions for training or paired troubleshooting — exclude those known scenarios.
investigation_steps: Identify both sessions' source IPs and users.
Confirm both are authorized.
response_guidance: Terminate any unconfirmed session immediately.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: iLO Remote Console Access Followed by BIOS Setting or Virtual Media Change
description: A Remote Console session is followed by a BIOS/RBSU configuration change or Virtual Media mount during the same session. This is the core high-priority console attack pattern this catalogue is built to catch: console access alone is a capability, but console access immediately preceding a security-relevant configuration change is a strong signal of active, hands-on-keyboard tampering.

data_sources.name: iLO Security Log
data_sources.description: Console session correlated with subsequent BIOS/virtual-media configuration events.

detection_logic: Correlates a console session-start event with a subsequent BIOS setting change or virtual media attach event on the same device within the session window.
spl:
index=ilo sourcetype=ilo_security
| eval stage=case(event="RemoteConsoleSessionStart","1_console_access", event="BIOSConfigChange" OR event="VirtualMediaAttached","2_config_change", 1==1, null())
| where isnotnull(stage)
| transaction host maxspan=30m startswith=eval(stage="1_console_access")
| where mvcount(mvdedup(stage))>=2
| table _time, host, user, stage
tuning_guidance: Legitimate during planned BIOS updates or OS deployment via mounted media — cross-reference against a change ticket before escalating.
investigation_steps: Identify exactly what BIOS setting or media was changed.
Confirm against a change ticket.
response_guidance: If unconfirmed, treat as active tampering: isolate the device from remote management and investigate immediately.
author: Threat Detection Library

threshold.baseline_condition: console session -> BIOS change or virtual media mount

title: iLO Remote Console Access Immediately Followed by Reboot
description: A Remote Console session is followed within minutes by a power-cycle/reset action on the same device — consistent with an operator making a BIOS/boot change interactively via console and then rebooting to apply it, which is exactly the workflow an attacker would use to weaken boot security and then reboot into the modified state.

data_sources.name: iLO Security Log
data_sources.description: Console session events correlated with subsequent power-action events.

detection_logic: Correlates a console session-start event with a subsequent power-cycle/reset event on the same device within 15 minutes.
spl:
index=ilo sourcetype=ilo_security
| eval stage=case(event="RemoteConsoleSessionStart","1_console_access", event="PowerControl" AND (action="Reset" OR action="PowerCycle"),"2_reboot", 1==1, null())
| where isnotnull(stage)
| transaction host maxspan=15m startswith=eval(stage="1_console_access")
| where mvcount(mvdedup(stage))>=2
| table _time, host, user, stage
tuning_guidance: Common, benign pattern during routine maintenance (applying an update, changing a setting) — pair with RC-004 (config change) to raise confidence this was a security-relevant change rather than routine work.
investigation_steps: Check whether a boot configuration or BIOS change occurred during the console session (RC-004, FW-###).
response_guidance: Investigate further if combined with an unconfirmed console session or a boot/BIOS change; otherwise treat as routine.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Unusually Long iLO Remote Console Session
description: A Remote Console session remains open significantly longer than typical maintenance activity for the device — a soft signal that may indicate the console is being used for extended interactive access (e.g. active reconnaissance or staged multi-step tampering) rather than a discrete maintenance task.

data_sources.name: iLO Security Log
data_sources.description: Session start/end pairs with computed duration.

detection_logic: Computes session duration from paired start/end events and flags outliers against the device's own historical baseline.
spl:
index=ilo sourcetype=ilo_security (event="RemoteConsoleSessionStart" OR event="RemoteConsoleSessionEnd")
| transaction host user maxevents=2
| eval duration_min=round(duration/60,1)
| where duration_min>=120
tuning_guidance: Some legitimate OS installation/deployment workflows via console genuinely take hours — exclude known deployment automation patterns.
investigation_steps: Review what activity occurred throughout the session if other detections fired during it.
response_guidance: Use as a contributing signal only; not independently actionable.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: iLO Remote Console Access to Newly Created Account's First Session
description: The named high-priority sequence from the specification: an administrator login is followed by creation of a new privileged user, and that new account's very first action is opening a Remote Console session. This pattern — create an account, then immediately use it for hands-on-keyboard access — is far more consistent with an attacker planting and immediately using a persistence account than with routine provisioning, where a new account's first login is typically a password-change/verification step, not a console session.

data_sources.name: iLO Security Log
data_sources.description: Admin login, new-user creation, and console session events correlated by acting/new identity.

detection_logic: Correlates an admin login, a subsequent new-user creation event, and a Remote Console session opened by that new user, all within 30 minutes.
spl:
index=ilo sourcetype=ilo_security
| eval stage=case(event="Login" AND result="Success","1_admin_login", event="UserAdded","2_new_user", event="RemoteConsoleSessionStart","3_console_by_new_user", 1==1, null())
| where isnotnull(stage)
| transaction host maxspan=30m startswith=eval(stage="1_admin_login")
| where mvcount(mvdedup(stage))>=3
| table _time, host, acting_user, user, stage
tuning_guidance: Legitimate for a newly-hired administrator's supervised first session — cross-reference against onboarding records before escalating.
investigation_steps: Identify the new account and the console session's activity.
Verify the account creation against a change ticket.
response_guidance: Treat as a confirmed persistence-and-use pattern if unconfirmed: disable the account and terminate the session immediately.
author: Threat Detection Library

threshold.baseline_condition: admin login -> new privileged user -> remote console by new user

title: iLO Virtual Media Attached
description: A virtual CD/DVD, USB image, or floppy is attached via iLO's Virtual Media capability, presenting it to the host operating system exactly as a physically-inserted device would. This is treated as a potential payload-delivery/OS-bypass mechanism throughout this catalogue: it lets an operator (or attacker) introduce arbitrary bootable or file-system content to the server without ever touching the datacenter floor.

data_sources.name: iLO Security Log
data_sources.description: Virtual media attach events with source URI/image.

detection_logic: Filters the iLO security log for virtual media attach events.
spl:
index=ilo sourcetype=ilo_security event="VirtualMediaAttached"
| table _time, host, user, media_type, source_uri
tuning_guidance: Baseline expected deployment-automation source URIs (e.g. a known OS-deployment image repository or Intelligent Provisioning) separately from ad hoc interactive mounts.
investigation_steps: Identify the source_uri — is it a known, trusted image repository?
Check whether a boot-order change and reboot followed (VMEDIA-002/RC-004).
response_guidance: If unconfirmed, treat as a potential payload-delivery attempt: detach the media and investigate the mounting session immediately.
author: Threat Detection Library
attack_mapping_note: ATT&CK has no dedicated technique for remotely-mounted virtual/emulated media specifically. T1200 (Hardware Additions) is the closest documented analogue — an iLO-mounted virtual CD/USB image is presented to the host exactly as a physically-inserted device would be, achieving the same effect (introducing attacker-controlled media the OS will recognize) without physical presence. Used here with this explicit caveat per specification quality-control rule #6.

title: iLO Virtual Media From Unusual or External URI
description: A virtual media attach event references a source URI outside the organization's known, approved image repositories — particularly one resolving to an external network. Since the mounted image is fetched by iLO itself (typically over HTTP/HTTPS), an externally-hosted image is functionally equivalent to an attacker delivering a payload directly onto the server's virtual media bus.

data_sources.name: iLO Security Log
data_sources.description: Virtual media attach events with source URI, cross-referenced against an approved-repository allowlist.

detection_logic: Joins virtual media attach events against a maintained allowlist of approved image repository hostnames/CIDR ranges.
spl:
index=ilo sourcetype=ilo_security event="VirtualMediaAttached"
| rex field=source_uri "://(?<uri_host>[^/]+)"
| lookup ilo_approved_media_sources.csv uri_host OUTPUT is_approved
| where isnull(is_approved)
| table _time, host, user, source_uri, uri_host
tuning_guidance: Maintain the approved-repository allowlist tightly — this should be a small, well-known set of internal deployment servers.
investigation_steps: Treat as a live incident pending confirmation.
Identify the URI's ownership and reachability.
response_guidance: Detach the media immediately and isolate the device from remote management if the source is unconfirmed or external.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1105: Ingress Tool Transfer

author: Threat Detection Library

title: iLO Virtual Media Mount Followed by One-Time Boot Override and Reboot
description: The flagship attack chain this catalogue is built around, named explicitly by the specification as the highest priority available: a virtual media mount, followed by a one-time boot-device override pointing at that media, followed by a reboot. This sequence lets an attacker boot the server directly into attacker-controlled media — bypassing the installed operating system, its authentication, its logging, and any endpoint protection running on it entirely.

data_sources.name: iLO Security Log
data_sources.description: Virtual media, boot-override, and power-action events for the same device within a short window.

detection_logic: Correlates a virtual media attach event with a subsequent one-time boot-override event targeting virtual media, followed by a power-cycle/reset, all on the same device within 20 minutes.
spl:
index=ilo sourcetype=ilo_security
| eval stage=case(event="VirtualMediaAttached","1_media_mounted", event="BootOverride" AND boot_device IN ("VirtualCD","VirtualUSB","VirtualFloppy"),"2_boot_override", event="PowerControl" AND (action="Reset" OR action="PowerCycle"),"3_reboot", 1==1, null())
| where isnotnull(stage)
| transaction host maxspan=20m startswith=eval(stage="1_media_mounted")
| where mvcount(mvdedup(stage))>=3
| table _time, host, user, stage
tuning_guidance: Legitimate for planned OS installation/recovery workflows — require this exact sequence to correlate with a change ticket; treat any unticketed occurrence as an emergency regardless of time of day.
investigation_steps: Treat as a live incident: the server may currently be booted into attacker-controlled media.
Do not assume the installed OS is still trustworthy once this sequence completes unconfirmed.
response_guidance: Power off the device immediately if the sequence is unconfirmed, detach the media, and treat the host OS as compromised pending full forensic imaging — a full rebuild may be warranted depending on findings.
author: Threat Detection Library

threshold.baseline_condition: virtual media mount -> one-time boot override to media -> reboot

title: iLO Virtual Media Mounted by Unusual Administrator
description: A virtual media attach event is performed by an account not on the small, expected list of administrators who routinely handle OS deployment/recovery media mounts for this device.

data_sources.name: iLO Security Log
data_sources.description: Virtual media events cross-referenced against an expected-operator baseline.

detection_logic: Joins virtual media attach events against a lookup of accounts expected to perform media operations.
spl:
index=ilo sourcetype=ilo_security event="VirtualMediaAttached"
| lookup ilo_media_operators.csv user OUTPUT is_expected_operator
| where isnull(is_expected_operator)
| table _time, host, user, source_uri
tuning_guidance: Maintain the expected-operator lookup; particularly valuable in larger environments where media operations are normally handled by a small deployment/imaging team.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification with the account owner.
response_guidance: Investigate if unconfirmed; treat consistently with VMEDIA-002 if the account is also unfamiliar.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: iLO Virtual Media Mounted Across Multiple Fleet Devices
description: The same virtual media image (identified by source_uri or filename) is mounted across an unusually large number of distinct iLO-managed servers within a short window — consistent with either a legitimate fleet-wide OS deployment campaign or an attacker who has scripted the same payload-delivery step across many hosts at once via a compromised shared credential or HPE OneView/Compute Ops Management access.

data_sources.name: iLO Security Log (fleet-aggregated)
data_sources.path: iLO Security Log, aggregated across devices
data_sources.description: Virtual media attach events across the managed fleet.

detection_logic: Counts distinct devices with a virtual media mount referencing the same source_uri in a rolling window.
spl:
index=ilo sourcetype=ilo_security event="VirtualMediaAttached"
| bin _time span=1h
| stats dc(host) as distinct_devices, values(host) as devices by source_uri, user, _time
| where distinct_devices>=5
tuning_guidance: Baseline your organization's normal fleet-deployment scope (scheduled OS reimaging campaigns will legitimately trigger this) and tune the threshold accordingly.
investigation_steps: Confirm against a change ticket for planned fleet-wide deployment.
Verify the source_uri against the approved-repository allowlist (VMEDIA-002).
response_guidance: If unauthorized, treat as a fleet-wide incident: identify every affected device and detach the media across all of them.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: iLO Remote Power Off/Cycle Command Issued
description: An iLO virtual power control command (off, cycle, cold boot, press-and-hold) was issued. Individually routine for maintenance, but high-value as a building block for destructive-attack correlation (unexpected power events combined with prior anomalous access, storage changes, or firmware changes).

data_sources.name: iLO Security Log
data_sources.description: Virtual power control action events.

detection_logic: Filters the iLO log for virtual power control events and surfaces the actor and action.
spl:
index=ilo sourcetype=ilo_security event="VirtualPowerControl"
| table _time, host, user, power_action, src_ip
tuning_guidance: Not alertable alone at scale; feed into ILO-018/ILO-019 and HPE-X sequences rather than alerting on every occurrence.
investigation_steps: Correlate with change management for planned maintenance windows.
response_guidance: No independent response; investigate as part of correlated sequences.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: iLO Power Control Outside Maintenance Window
description: A virtual power control action occurs outside any declared maintenance window and outside the device's learned normal-operating-hours baseline for power events, consistent with disruptive or unauthorized use of out-of-band power control.

data_sources.name: iLO Security Log
data_sources.description: Power control events cross-referenced against a maintenance calendar lookup.

detection_logic: Filters power control events where a maintenance-window lookup does not cover the event time.
spl:
index=ilo sourcetype=ilo_security event="VirtualPowerControl"
| lookup maintenance_windows.csv host, _time OUTPUT in_window
| where isnull(in_window) OR in_window=0
| table _time, host, user, power_action
tuning_guidance: Requires a maintained maintenance-window lookup; without one, baseline per-host normal hours instead and expect a higher false-positive rate.
investigation_steps: Confirm with the device owner whether the action was authorized.
Check for concurrent Remote Console or Virtual Media activity.
response_guidance: If unconfirmed, treat as unauthorized disruption; investigate the source account and IP.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: iLO Repeated Power Cycling of Same Host (Denial of Availability)
description: The same host receives three or more virtual power control actions within a short window, consistent with an attacker forcing repeated reboots to disrupt availability, interfere with a boot-time attack sequence, or force the host into a manipulated boot path (e.g. one-time boot override).

data_sources.name: iLO Security Log
data_sources.description: Repeated power control events for a single host.

detection_logic: Counts power control events per host in a rolling window and flags hosts over threshold.
spl:
index=ilo sourcetype=ilo_security event="VirtualPowerControl"
| bin _time span=15m
| stats count as power_events by host, _time
| where power_events>=3
tuning_guidance: Exclude hosts under known automated test/CI power-cycling harnesses via an allowlist.
investigation_steps: Check for concurrent boot configuration or firmware changes.
Identify the account(s) performing the cycling.
response_guidance: Treat as an active availability incident; contact the device owner and consider disabling the acting account pending review.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: iLO Cold Boot / Press-and-Hold Reset Issued to Production Host
description: A hard/cold power reset (bypassing graceful OS shutdown) was issued via iLO to a host tagged as production, which can cause data loss or corruption on the running workload and may indicate either an emergency response or an attacker attempting to force an ungraceful state.

data_sources.name: iLO Security Log
data_sources.description: Cold-boot/press-and-hold power events cross-referenced with an asset-criticality lookup.

detection_logic: Filters for the cold-boot/press-and-hold power action and joins against a criticality lookup for production tagging.
spl:
index=ilo sourcetype=ilo_security event="VirtualPowerControl" power_action="ColdBoot"
| lookup asset_criticality.csv host OUTPUT tier
| where tier="production"
| table _time, host, user, power_action
tuning_guidance: Requires an asset-criticality lookup; tune out approved emergency-response accounts/runbooks.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification immediately with the on-call owner.
response_guidance: Validate host integrity after the event; escalate if unconfirmed.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: iLO One-Time Boot Override Set
description: A one-time boot device override was configured via iLO (e.g. to Virtual Media, PXE, or USB). This is the pivotal step in the highest-priority iLO attack chain: virtual media mount followed by a boot override and reboot lets an attacker boot arbitrary attacker-controlled media, bypassing the installed OS and any of its controls entirely.

data_sources.name: iLO Security Log
data_sources.description: Boot source override configuration events.

detection_logic: Filters the iLO log for one-time boot override configuration events.
spl:
index=ilo sourcetype=ilo_security event="OneTimeBootOverrideSet"
| table _time, host, user, boot_target, src_ip
tuning_guidance: Low expected volume outside of imaging/recovery workflows; alert on all occurrences and correlate with VMEDIA-003.
investigation_steps: Immediately check for a concurrent or preceding Virtual Media attach (VMEDIA-###).
Confirm business justification for the boot target chosen.
response_guidance: Treat unconfirmed occurrences as a likely precursor to OS bypass; consider powering off the host before the next boot completes if unconfirmed.
author: Threat Detection Library
attack_mapping_note: ATT&CK T1542 (Pre-OS Boot) is the closest-fit technique for boot-source-override abuse; it is used here despite iLO boot override being a management-plane action rather than a direct pre-OS boot-component modification, because the effect (attacker controls what boots next) is functionally equivalent.

title: iLO Boot Order Permanently Changed
description: The persistent (not one-time) boot order was modified via iLO/RBSU, changing what the host boots from on every subsequent restart. Unlike a one-time override, this represents durable persistence and warrants a higher scrutiny bar.

data_sources.name: iLO Security Log
data_sources.description: Persistent boot order change events.

detection_logic: Filters the iLO log for persistent boot-order-change events.
spl:
index=ilo sourcetype=ilo_security event="BootOrderChanged"
| table _time, host, user, new_boot_order
tuning_guidance: Expected during initial provisioning; tune out the imaging window and alert on changes to already-in-service hosts.
investigation_steps: Compare new_boot_order against the expected baseline for the host's role.
Confirm change ticket.
response_guidance: Revert unauthorized changes and investigate the acting account for broader compromise.
author: Threat Detection Library
attack_mapping_note: ATT&CK T1542 (Pre-OS Boot) used as closest-fit technique for persistent boot-order tampering via the management plane.

title: iLO Network Boot (PXE) Enabled on Production Host
description: PXE/network boot was enabled via iLO on a host tagged as production, expanding the host's attack surface to include rogue DHCP/PXE server compromise as a boot-time attack vector.

data_sources.name: iLO Security Log
data_sources.description: Boot configuration change events indicating PXE enablement.

detection_logic: Filters boot configuration change events where PXE/network boot is enabled, joined to a production-tagging lookup.
spl:
index=ilo sourcetype=ilo_security event="BootConfigChanged" boot_setting="NetworkBootEnabled"
| lookup asset_criticality.csv host OUTPUT tier
| where tier="production"
| table _time, host, user
tuning_guidance: Legitimate for imaging fleets; tune out hosts under active provisioning.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification.
Verify the PXE/DHCP environment is trusted and segmented.
response_guidance: Disable if unconfirmed; low individual urgency but escalate if combined with other boot-tampering indicators.
author: Threat Detection Library
attack_mapping_note: ATT&CK T1542 (Pre-OS Boot) used as closest-fit; PXE enablement alone is a low-confidence precursor rather than a direct exploitation technique.

title: iLO Secure Boot Disabled
description: UEFI Secure Boot was disabled via iLO/RBSU. This removes a foundational boot-integrity control and is a hallmark step of firmware/bootkit-level persistence attempts; there is essentially no routine reason to disable it on an in-service production host.

data_sources.name: iLO Security Log
data_sources.description: UEFI Secure Boot state-change events.

detection_logic: Filters BIOS/UEFI setting-change events for Secure Boot transitioning to disabled.
spl:
index=ilo sourcetype=ilo_security event="BiosSettingChanged" setting="SecureBoot" new_value="Disabled"
| table _time, host, user, src_ip
tuning_guidance: Alert on every occurrence; the extremely small set of legitimate cases (e.g. certain legacy OS installs) should go through an explicit change-ticket allowlist rather than broad tuning.
investigation_steps: Treat as a live incident.
Check for concurrent firmware downgrade (FW-005) or TPM changes (FW-002).
Verify with the host owner before any reboot occurs.
response_guidance: Re-enable Secure Boot immediately if unconfirmed, and treat the host as a candidate for firmware-level compromise pending validation of boot component integrity.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: iLO TPM Configuration Changed or Cleared
description: The Trusted Platform Module was reconfigured, disabled, or cleared via iLO/RBSU. TPM clearing destroys the measured-boot chain of trust and any TPM-sealed secrets (e.g. disk encryption keys), and is a step consistent with defeating measured-boot-based integrity verification.

data_sources.name: iLO Security Log
data_sources.description: TPM setting-change or clear events.

detection_logic: Filters for TPM configuration or clear events.
spl:
index=ilo sourcetype=ilo_security event="TpmConfigChanged" OR event="TpmCleared"
| table _time, host, user, action
tuning_guidance: Alert on every occurrence; require an explicit pre-approved change ticket for any legitimate TPM clear (e.g. hardware replacement).
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification immediately.
Check whether disk encryption on the host depends on this TPM.
response_guidance: Halt any pending reboot if unconfirmed; a cleared TPM can render disk-encrypted volumes inaccessible or, if attacker-driven, enable a fresh trust chain the attacker controls.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: iLO BIOS/UEFI Administrator Password Changed or Removed
description: The BIOS/UEFI (RBSU) administrator password was changed or removed via iLO, which controls who can subsequently alter boot/firmware/security settings directly at POST, independent of iLO credentials.

data_sources.name: iLO Security Log
data_sources.description: BIOS admin password change events.

detection_logic: Filters for BIOS administrator password change/removal events.
spl:
index=ilo sourcetype=ilo_security event="BiosAdminPasswordChanged"
| table _time, host, user, action
tuning_guidance: Low volume; alert on all occurrences outside a documented credential-rotation window.
investigation_steps: Confirm with the requesting administrator.
Check whether this follows a suspicious iLO login (ILO-004).
response_guidance: Reset to a known-good password under dual control if unconfirmed.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: iLO Physical Presence / Intrusion Detection Alarm
description: The chassis intrusion-detection switch reported an open/tamper event, which is the closest signal HPE server hardware provides to physical tampering, relevant to hardware implant or direct console/firmware attacks that bypass iLO/network controls entirely.

data_sources.name: IML
data_sources.description: Chassis intrusion / physical-tamper events.

detection_logic: Filters IML events for chassis-intrusion-detection alarms.
spl:
index=ilo sourcetype=ilo_iml event="ChassisIntrusionDetected"
| table _time, host, event_type
tuning_guidance: Expect occasional legitimate hardware-maintenance triggers; correlate with change tickets for planned hardware service.
investigation_steps: Confirm with data-center operations whether authorized physical access occurred.
Check for any subsequent firmware or BIOS setting changes.
response_guidance: Physically inspect the host if unconfirmed; treat as a potential hardware-implant scenario.
author: Threat Detection Library
attack_mapping_note: ATT&CK T1200 (Hardware Additions) used as closest-fit; chassis intrusion detection is a physical-tamper signal rather than a direct hardware-addition technique.

title: iLO Firmware Downgrade Detected
description: An iLO, BIOS, or component firmware update installed a version lower than the currently running version. Firmware downgrade is a well-established technique to reintroduce known vulnerabilities or strip security mitigations added in later firmware, and is treated as suspicious by default in this library regardless of stated justification.

data_sources.name: iLO Security Log
data_sources.description: Firmware update events with before/after version.

detection_logic: Compares old_version and new_version on firmware update events and flags any decrease.
spl:
index=ilo sourcetype=ilo_security event="FirmwareUpdate"
| eval downgrade=if(old_version>new_version, 1, 0)
| where downgrade=1
| table _time, host, user, component, old_version, new_version
tuning_guidance: Requires a version-comparison approach appropriate to the actual firmware versioning scheme in use (semantic-version comparison is illustrative here); alert on every confirmed downgrade.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification (rare: recovery from a bad firmware release).
Identify who initiated the update and from what source (local file vs. remote URL).
response_guidance: Revert to the latest known-good firmware if unconfirmed and audit the host for any activity that occurred while running the downgraded firmware.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: iLO Firmware Update From Unusual/External Source
description: A firmware update was applied from a source URI/location outside the organization's approved firmware repository, raising the possibility of a supply-chain or trojanized-firmware attack via the OOB management plane.

data_sources.name: iLO Security Log
data_sources.description: Firmware update source location.

detection_logic: Joins firmware update events against an allowlist of approved firmware repository locations.
spl:
index=ilo sourcetype=ilo_security event="FirmwareUpdate"
| lookup approved_firmware_sources.csv source_uri OUTPUT is_approved
| where isnull(is_approved)
| table _time, host, user, component, source_uri
tuning_guidance: Maintain the approved-source allowlist; expected to be a small, stable list (HPE SPP repository, internal mirror).
investigation_steps: Verify the source_uri and, if possible, the firmware image hash against HPE-published checksums.
response_guidance: Do not allow the update to complete if in progress and unconfirmed; if already applied, treat the host as compromised pending validation.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: iLO Firmware Update Outside Maintenance Window
description: A firmware update occurred outside any declared maintenance window, which is unusual given that firmware updates typically require careful scheduling around workload impact.

data_sources.name: iLO Security Log
data_sources.description: Firmware update events cross-referenced against a maintenance calendar.

detection_logic: Filters firmware update events where a maintenance-window lookup does not cover the event time.
spl:
index=ilo sourcetype=ilo_security event="FirmwareUpdate"
| lookup maintenance_windows.csv host, _time OUTPUT in_window
| where isnull(in_window) OR in_window=0
| table _time, host, user, component
tuning_guidance: Requires a maintained maintenance-window lookup.
investigation_steps: Confirm with the change process.
Cross-reference with FW-005/FW-006 for downgrade or untrusted-source indicators.
response_guidance: Investigate if unconfirmed; not independently urgent unless correlated with other firmware indicators.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: iLO Firmware Rollback Protection Disabled
description: A setting controlling firmware anti-rollback/downgrade protection was disabled via iLO, which is a prerequisite step an attacker would need before successfully applying a malicious firmware downgrade (FW-005).

data_sources.name: iLO Security Log
data_sources.description: Firmware protection setting-change events.

detection_logic: Filters for the specific setting change disabling firmware downgrade/rollback protection.
spl:
index=ilo sourcetype=ilo_security event="SecuritySettingChanged" setting="FirmwareRollbackProtection" new_value="Disabled"
| table _time, host, user, src_ip
tuning_guidance: Alert on every occurrence; essentially no routine reason to disable this on an in-service host.
investigation_steps: Treat as a likely precursor to FW-005.
Confirm business justification immediately.
response_guidance: Re-enable immediately if unconfirmed and monitor closely for a subsequent firmware update.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Redfish API Authentication Failure Threshold
description: Repeated Redfish API authentication failures against a single iLO device, consistent with credential-stuffing or brute-force attempts against the REST management API rather than the web/SSH interface.

data_sources.name: iLO Redfish Audit
data_sources.description: Redfish session authentication attempts.

detection_logic: Counts failed Redfish session-creation attempts per host/IP in a rolling window.
spl:
index=ilo sourcetype=ilo_redfish event="SessionAuthentication" result="Failed"
| bin _time span=10m
| stats count as failures by host, src_ip, _time
| where failures>=5
tuning_guidance: Tune against known automation/orchestration tool source IPs with occasional transient credential-rotation failures.
investigation_steps: Identify the source IP and correlate with other Redfish/iLO activity from the same source.
response_guidance: Block the source IP at the OOB management network boundary if unconfirmed; rotate credentials if a valid account is implicated.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Redfish API Configuration Change to Security-Relevant Resource
description: A PATCH/POST/DELETE Redfish API call modified a security-relevant resource (e.g. AccountService, SecurityService, Manager NetworkProtocol) directly via the REST API rather than the web UI, which is the typical path for scripted/automated attacks and API-token abuse.

data_sources.name: iLO Redfish Audit
data_sources.description: Redfish write requests to security-relevant resource paths.

detection_logic: Filters Redfish write methods (PATCH/POST/DELETE) against a list of security-sensitive resource path prefixes.
spl:
index=ilo sourcetype=ilo_redfish (method="PATCH" OR method="POST" OR method="DELETE")
| where match(resource_path, "(?i)(AccountService|SecurityService|NetworkProtocol|Certificates)")
| table _time, host, user, method, resource_path, src_ip
tuning_guidance: Expected during legitimate automation-driven configuration management; allowlist known IaC/orchestration service accounts and tune for the remainder.
investigation_steps: Identify the calling account/token and correlate with recent authentication events (HREDFISH-001, ILO-008).
response_guidance: Review the specific change made and revert if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Redfish API Token/Session Created With Extended Lifetime
description: A Redfish session or API token was created with a non-default, extended expiration/lifetime, which could support long-lived unattended access outside normal session-timeout controls.

data_sources.name: iLO Redfish Audit
data_sources.description: Session lifetime parameter at creation.

detection_logic: Filters Redfish session-creation events where the requested timeout exceeds the organizational default.
spl:
index=ilo sourcetype=ilo_redfish event="SessionCreated"
| where session_timeout > 1800
| table _time, host, user, session_timeout, src_ip
tuning_guidance: Tune the threshold to the organization's standard session-timeout policy.
investigation_steps: Confirm the requesting account and business justification for an extended session.
response_guidance: Terminate the session if unconfirmed and review the account's recent activity.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Redfish API Access From Non-Standard Client/User-Agent
description: Redfish API calls are observed with a user-agent string outside the small set of expected automation tools (e.g. iLO Amplifier, Ansible/Redfish modules, OneView), which may indicate reconnaissance or scripted abuse using a custom or off-the-shelf attack tool.

data_sources.name: iLO Redfish Audit
data_sources.description: User-agent field on API requests.

detection_logic: Joins Redfish request events against a lookup of expected user-agent strings and flags misses.
spl:
index=ilo sourcetype=ilo_redfish
| lookup expected_redfish_agents.csv user_agent OUTPUT is_expected
| where isnull(is_expected)
| stats count by host, user_agent, src_ip
tuning_guidance: Maintain the expected-agent lookup; high false-positive rate until tuned to the environment's actual tooling.
investigation_steps: Identify the tool/script behind the unusual user-agent.
response_guidance: Low individual urgency; use as a discovery signal feeding correlation searches.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1082: System Information Discovery

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Redfish EventService Subscription Deleted
description: A Redfish EventService subscription (used to forward iLO events/alerts to external listeners such as SIEM or monitoring integrations) was deleted, which can silently break external alerting for the device.

data_sources.name: iLO Redfish Audit
data_sources.description: Subscription delete events.

detection_logic: Filters Redfish EventService subscription-delete events.
spl:
index=ilo sourcetype=ilo_redfish event="EventSubscriptionDeleted"
| table _time, host, user, subscription_destination
tuning_guidance: Low volume; alert on all occurrences and verify against monitoring/SIEM integration inventories.
investigation_steps: Confirm whether the destination is a decommissioned or an active monitoring endpoint.
response_guidance: Re-create the subscription if unauthorized; investigate the acting account.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Redfish API Used to Enumerate All Systems/Chassis Resources at Scale
description: A single account/source generates a high volume of Redfish GET requests against Systems/Chassis/Managers resources across many distinct iLO-managed hosts in a short window, consistent with automated fleet-wide reconnaissance ahead of a targeted attack.

data_sources.name: iLO Redfish Audit (fleet-aggregated)
data_sources.path: Redfish API request log, aggregated across devices
data_sources.description: GET requests to inventory/discovery resource paths.

detection_logic: Counts distinct hosts queried by the same account/source within a rolling window.
spl:
index=ilo sourcetype=ilo_redfish method="GET"
| where match(resource_path, "(?i)(Systems|Chassis|Managers)")
| bin _time span=1h
| stats dc(host) as distinct_hosts by user, src_ip, _time
| where distinct_hosts>=20
tuning_guidance: Tune out known inventory/CMDB-sync automation accounts.
investigation_steps: Identify the source and confirm against known fleet-management tooling.
response_guidance: Investigate the account if not attributable to approved tooling; consider read-only credential misuse.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1082: System Information Discovery

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Redfish API BIOS/Boot Resource Modified via PATCH
description: A Redfish PATCH request modified the Bios or Boot resource directly via the REST API, which is the programmatic equivalent of the RBSU changes covered by FW-001/ILO-021/ILO-022 and is the path a scripted attack would most likely use.

data_sources.name: iLO Redfish Audit
data_sources.description: PATCH requests to Bios/Boot resource paths.

detection_logic: Filters Redfish PATCH requests to Bios or Boot resource paths.
spl:
index=ilo sourcetype=ilo_redfish method="PATCH"
| where match(resource_path, "(?i)/(Bios|Boot)")
| table _time, host, user, resource_path, body, src_ip
tuning_guidance: Correlate directly with FW-001, ILO-021, and ILO-022; treat as the same event class regardless of whether it was made via UI or API.
investigation_steps: Inspect the request body for the specific setting changed.
response_guidance: Same as FW-001/ILO-021 depending on the specific setting affected.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Redfish API Call Preceding Fleet-Wide Configuration Push
description: A Redfish discovery/enumeration burst (HREDFISH-006) is immediately followed by the same account issuing configuration-write (PATCH/POST) calls against a large number of the same discovered hosts, consistent with a scripted attack that enumerates then mass-modifies fleet configuration.

data_sources.name: iLO Redfish Audit (fleet-aggregated)
data_sources.path: Redfish API request log, aggregated across devices
data_sources.description: Discovery burst followed by write burst from the same account.

detection_logic: Sequences a discovery burst and a subsequent write burst from the same account within a bounded window.
spl:
index=ilo sourcetype=ilo_redfish
| eval stage=case(method="GET", "1_discovery", method="PATCH" OR method="POST", "2_write", true(), null())
| where isnotnull(stage)
| transaction user maxspan=1h startswith=eval(stage="1_discovery")
| where mvcount(mvdedup(stage))>=2 AND dc(host)>=10
| table _time, user, dc_host, eventcount
tuning_guidance: Requires environment-specific tuning of the discovery/write thresholds; high-value once tuned given the fleet-wide blast radius.
investigation_steps: Identify all affected hosts and the specific configuration pushed.
Confirm against a change ticket for planned fleet-wide configuration management.
response_guidance: Treat as a fleet-wide incident if unconfirmed; halt further automation runs from the account pending review.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1082: System Information Discovery

author: Threat Detection Library

title: iLO Dedicated Management Network Interface Changed to Shared
description: The iLO network mode was changed from Dedicated (isolated OOB port) to Shared (uses a production NIC), which materially widens the attack surface for the management interface by exposing it on the same network as production traffic.

data_sources.name: iLO Security Log
data_sources.description: Network mode configuration change events.

detection_logic: Filters network configuration change events where network_mode transitions to Shared.
spl:
index=ilo sourcetype=ilo_security event="NetworkModeChanged" network_mode="Shared"
| table _time, host, user, src_ip
tuning_guidance: Rare in a properly segmented environment; alert on all occurrences.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification.
Verify current network segmentation policy is being followed.
response_guidance: Revert to Dedicated mode if unauthorized.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1599: Network Boundary Bridging

author: Threat Detection Library
attack_mapping_note: ATT&CK T1599 (Network Boundary Bridging) used as closest-fit; this is a management-plane network-exposure change rather than a direct boundary-bridging technique.

title: iLO Access Control List / IP Restriction Removed or Weakened
description: An IP-based access restriction list controlling which source addresses may reach the iLO interface was removed or weakened, potentially exposing the management plane to a broader network.

data_sources.name: iLO Security Log
data_sources.description: Access control list configuration change events.

detection_logic: Filters access-control-list configuration change events indicating removal or weakening.
spl:
index=ilo sourcetype=ilo_security event="AccessControlListChanged" action="Removed"
| table _time, host, user, src_ip
tuning_guidance: Alert on all occurrences outside a documented network-change window.
investigation_steps: Confirm justification.
Check for subsequent login attempts from previously blocked ranges.
response_guidance: Restore restrictions if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: iLO DNS/NTP Server Configuration Changed
description: The iLO's configured DNS or NTP servers were changed. Attacker-controlled DNS can redirect firmware-update or certificate-validation lookups; attacker-controlled NTP can skew timestamps to undermine log correlation and forensic timelines.

data_sources.name: iLO Security Log
data_sources.description: DNS/NTP configuration change events.

detection_logic: Filters configuration change events for the DNS/NTP server settings.
spl:
index=ilo sourcetype=ilo_security event="NetworkConfigChanged" (setting="DnsServer" OR setting="NtpServer")
| table _time, host, user, setting, new_value
tuning_guidance: Expected during initial provisioning or planned infrastructure migration; tune out the provisioning window.
investigation_steps: Verify the new server against the organization's approved DNS/NTP infrastructure.
response_guidance: Revert if the new value is unrecognized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: iLO Insecure Management Protocol Enabled
description: A legacy/insecure management protocol (e.g. Telnet, unencrypted SNMP v1/v2c write access, or IPMI over LAN) was enabled on iLO, reintroducing an unauthenticated or weakly-authenticated management path.

data_sources.name: iLO Security Log
data_sources.description: Management protocol enablement events.

detection_logic: Filters configuration change events enabling a protocol on the organization's disallowed-legacy-protocol list.
spl:
index=ilo sourcetype=ilo_security event="ManagementProtocolChanged" action="Enabled"
| lookup disallowed_legacy_protocols.csv protocol OUTPUT is_disallowed
| where is_disallowed=1
| table _time, host, user, protocol
tuning_guidance: Maintain the disallowed-protocol lookup to match organizational hardening standards.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification (rare: legacy tooling compatibility).
response_guidance: Disable the protocol if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: iLO IPMI Enabled
description: IPMI over LAN was enabled on iLO. IPMI has a well-documented history of authentication weaknesses (e.g. cipher-zero, predictable password-hash disclosure) and is generally recommended to remain disabled unless a specific legacy tool requires it.

data_sources.name: iLO Security Log
data_sources.description: IPMI-over-LAN enablement events.

detection_logic: Filters configuration change events enabling IPMI over LAN.
spl:
index=ilo sourcetype=ilo_security event="IpmiOverLanChanged" action="Enabled"
| table _time, host, user, src_ip
tuning_guidance: Alert on all occurrences given IPMI's known weaknesses; treat as a hardening-standard violation.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification and, if approved, ensure network access is tightly restricted.
response_guidance: Disable unless explicitly required and compensating network controls are in place.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: iLO Federation/Group Management Membership Changed
description: Device membership in an iLO Federation group changed. Federation groups allow a single set of credentials/permissions to manage many iLO devices at once, so unauthorized membership changes can dramatically expand an attacker's blast radius across the fleet.

data_sources.name: iLO Security Log
data_sources.description: Federation group membership change events.

detection_logic: Filters federation group membership change events.
spl:
index=ilo sourcetype=ilo_security event="FederationGroupChanged"
| table _time, host, user, federation_group, action
tuning_guidance: Low volume; alert on all occurrences outside planned fleet-management changes.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification.
Enumerate all devices reachable via the affected federation group.
response_guidance: Revert if unauthorized and review all devices in the affected federation group for suspicious activity.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: iLO SSL/TLS Certificate Replaced
description: The iLO web/API SSL/TLS certificate was replaced. Legitimate during certificate rotation, but an attacker-installed certificate could support man-in-the-middle interception of subsequent management sessions or covertly disable certificate-pinning-based detection.

data_sources.name: iLO Security Log
data_sources.description: Certificate replacement events.

detection_logic: Filters certificate-replacement events and surfaces the new certificate's issuer/thumbprint for comparison against the approved CA.
spl:
index=ilo sourcetype=ilo_security event="CertificateReplaced"
| table _time, host, user, certificate_issuer, certificate_thumbprint
tuning_guidance: Expected during scheduled certificate rotation; tune out the organization's approved internal CA issuer and alert on any other issuer.
investigation_steps: Verify the certificate issuer against the organization's approved CA.
Confirm with the requesting administrator.
response_guidance: Revert to a certificate from the approved CA if the new certificate is unrecognized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: iLO Trusted CA Certificate Added (Directory/LDAPS)
description: A new CA certificate was added to iLO's trusted store for directory (LDAPS) authentication validation. An attacker-added trusted CA could allow a rogue directory server to be trusted for authentication decisions, undermining centralized identity controls.

data_sources.name: iLO Security Log
data_sources.description: Trusted CA certificate addition events.

detection_logic: Filters trusted-CA-addition events for the directory authentication trust store.
spl:
index=ilo sourcetype=ilo_security event="TrustedCaAdded" context="DirectoryAuthentication"
| table _time, host, user, certificate_issuer, certificate_thumbprint
tuning_guidance: Very low expected volume; alert on all occurrences.
investigation_steps: Verify against the organization's PKI change process.
response_guidance: Remove the untrusted CA immediately if unconfirmed and audit any authentications that occurred while it was trusted.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: iLO Client Certificate Authentication Disabled
description: Client (mutual TLS) certificate-based authentication for iLO was disabled, falling back to password-only authentication where a stronger factor had previously been required.

data_sources.name: iLO Security Log
data_sources.description: Client certificate authentication setting-change events.

detection_logic: Filters setting-change events disabling client certificate authentication.
spl:
index=ilo sourcetype=ilo_security event="SecuritySettingChanged" setting="ClientCertificateAuth" new_value="Disabled"
| table _time, host, user, src_ip
tuning_guidance: Alert on all occurrences in environments where client-certificate auth is a mandated control.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification.
response_guidance: Re-enable if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: iLO Syslog Forwarding Destination Changed
description: The remote syslog forwarding destination configured on iLO was changed. Redirecting syslog to an attacker-controlled or non-existent host is a classic anti-forensics move that silently blinds central log collection for this device.

data_sources.name: iLO Security Log
data_sources.description: Syslog destination configuration change events.

detection_logic: Filters syslog destination configuration change events and compares the new destination against the approved SIEM/collector allowlist.
spl:
index=ilo sourcetype=ilo_security event="SyslogDestinationChanged"
| lookup approved_siem_destinations.csv new_destination OUTPUT is_approved
| where isnull(is_approved)
| table _time, host, user, old_destination, new_destination
tuning_guidance: Very low expected volume; alert on all occurrences where the new destination is not the approved collector.
investigation_steps: Treat as a likely anti-forensics attempt.
Immediately pull the device's local IML/Security Log directly before further tampering can occur.
response_guidance: Restore the correct syslog destination immediately and treat any gap in forwarded logs as a period requiring direct-device log review.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: iLO Syslog Forwarding Disabled
description: Remote syslog forwarding was disabled entirely on iLO, cutting off centralized visibility into this device's activity going forward.

data_sources.name: iLO Security Log
data_sources.description: Syslog forwarding disablement events.

detection_logic: Filters for the syslog-forwarding-disabled event, which — being the very event that stops forwarding — should be alerted on primarily via the SIEM's own gap/heartbeat detection as a backstop (see ILO-035) in addition to this direct event.
spl:
index=ilo sourcetype=ilo_security event="SyslogForwardingDisabled"
| table _time, host, user, src_ip
tuning_guidance: Alert on all occurrences; treat with maximum urgency given the anti-forensics implication.
investigation_steps: Treat as a live incident.
Immediately pull the local Security Log/IML directly from the device.
response_guidance: Re-enable forwarding and escalate as a probable active compromise.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: iLO Device Missing From Expected Syslog Feed (Heartbeat Gap)
description: A device that normally forwards a baseline volume of iLO events has produced none for longer than its expected heartbeat interval, which can indicate log forwarding was silently disabled, redirected, or the device itself was powered off/disconnected — all of which merit investigation regardless of which occurred.

data_sources.name: iLO Security Log (fleet-aggregated)
data_sources.path: Fleet device inventory joined against last-seen event time
data_sources.description: Detects the absence of expected telemetry, not a specific event.

detection_logic: Compares each known iLO device's last event time against an expected heartbeat interval derived from its historical baseline.
spl:
| tstats latest(_time) as last_seen where index=ilo by host
| eval gap_hours=round((now()-last_seen)/3600,1)
| where gap_hours > 24
| table host, last_seen, gap_hours
tuning_guidance: Tune the gap threshold to the fleet's actual expected event cadence; devices under planned maintenance/power-down should be suppressed via a maintenance lookup.
investigation_steps: Determine whether the device is powered off, network-isolated, or has had logging disabled/redirected (ILO-033, ILO-034).
Physically or out-of-band verify device state if the gap is unexplained.
response_guidance: Escalate unexplained gaps as a probable anti-forensics indicator.
author: Threat Detection Library

threshold.baseline_condition: no events received from a previously-active device

title: iLO Local Security Log / IML Cleared
description: The local iLO Security Log or Integrated Management Log was manually cleared. This is one of the clearest available anti-forensics signals on the platform and should be treated with the highest priority regardless of stated justification.

data_sources.name: iLO Security Log / IML
data_sources.description: Log-clear events, which are themselves typically recorded as a distinct event even when the log they clear is wiped.

detection_logic: Filters for the log-clear event type across both the Security Log and IML.
spl:
index=ilo sourcetype=ilo_security event="LogCleared"
| table _time, host, user, log_type, src_ip
tuning_guidance: Alert on all occurrences; the very small set of legitimate cases (decommissioning, compliance-driven log rotation) should be exception-listed via change ticket rather than tuned broadly.
investigation_steps: Treat as a live incident.
Immediately check for any forwarded copies of the cleared log in the SIEM to reconstruct recent activity.
Identify every action taken by the clearing account in the period immediately before the clear.
response_guidance: Treat the device as compromised pending investigation; the log clear is very likely intended to hide a preceding malicious action.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: IML Critical Hardware Fault Logged
description: The Integrated Management Log recorded a critical hardware fault (e.g. memory, CPU, storage controller, power supply). While most causes are benign hardware failure, a cluster of faults across components can also indicate physical tampering or aggressive out-of-spec manipulation via management-plane commands.

data_sources.name: IML
data_sources.description: Critical-severity hardware fault entries.

detection_logic: Filters IML entries at critical severity.
spl:
index=ilo sourcetype=ilo_iml severity="Critical"
| table _time, host, component, description
tuning_guidance: Route to hardware/facilities operations by default; escalate to security only when correlated with other suspicious activity.
investigation_steps: Correlate with recent physical access or management-plane configuration changes.
response_guidance: Standard hardware-fault response; escalate to security if correlated with FW-004 or unusual account activity.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: IML Cleared
description: The Integrated Management Log was cleared. Duplicate coverage of ILO-036 scoped specifically to the IML data source for environments that ingest IML and iLO Security Log separately.

data_sources.name: IML
data_sources.description: Log-clear entry.

detection_logic: Filters IML entries indicating the log itself was cleared.
spl:
index=ilo sourcetype=ilo_iml event="LogCleared"
| table _time, host, user
tuning_guidance: Alert on all occurrences; exception-list only via change ticket.
investigation_steps: Same as ILO-036.
response_guidance: Same as ILO-036.
author: Threat Detection Library
