title: IML Repair/Maintenance Flag Set Without Corresponding Ticket
description: An IML entry was manually marked as repaired/acknowledged, which can be used to suppress an entry from active-alert views without actually clearing the log — a subtler alternative to a full IML clear.

data_sources.name: IML
data_sources.description: Entry acknowledgment/repair-flag events, joined against a change-ticket lookup.

detection_logic: Joins repair-flag events against a change-ticket lookup and flags unticketed occurrences at volume.
spl:
index=ilo sourcetype=ilo_iml event="EntryMarkedRepaired"
| lookup change_tickets.csv host, _time OUTPUT ticket_id
| where isnull(ticket_id)
| stats count by host, user
| where count>=5
tuning_guidance: High false-positive rate without a change-ticket lookup; treat as a low-priority supplementary signal.
investigation_steps: Confirm the entries acknowledged were legitimately resolved.
response_guidance: Low urgency; investigate if correlated with other anti-forensics indicators.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: IML Records Unexpected Server Reset/Power Loss Event
description: The IML recorded an unexpected reset or power-loss event not preceded by a graceful shutdown command, useful as an independent hardware-level corroboration of ILO-017/ILO-019 power-control activity, including cases where the power action itself was not captured (e.g. physical power-cable pull).

data_sources.name: IML
data_sources.description: Unexpected reset/power-loss entries.

detection_logic: Filters IML entries for unexpected reset/power-loss event types.
spl:
index=ilo sourcetype=ilo_iml event="UnexpectedReset"
| table _time, host, event_type
tuning_guidance: Correlate with ILO-017/ILO-019/ILO-020 to distinguish iLO-driven power actions from physical/PDU-level events.
investigation_steps: Check for a corresponding iLO virtual power control event; absence suggests a physical-layer event.
response_guidance: Investigate physical data-center access logs if no corresponding iLO event is found.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: IML Fan/Thermal Anomaly Coinciding With Firmware Change
description: A thermal or fan-control anomaly recorded in the IML occurs within a short window of a firmware update, which — while usually benign (post-update fan recalibration) — can occasionally indicate a malicious or corrupted firmware image affecting hardware-control behavior.

data_sources.name: IML + iLO Security Log
data_sources.path: IML thermal entries joined with FirmwareUpdate events
data_sources.description: Sequence of firmware update followed by thermal/fan anomaly.

detection_logic: Sequences a firmware update event with a subsequent thermal/fan anomaly IML entry on the same host within a bounded window.
spl:
index=ilo (sourcetype=ilo_iml event="ThermalAnomaly") OR (sourcetype=ilo_security event="FirmwareUpdate")
| eval stage=case(event="FirmwareUpdate","1_update", event="ThermalAnomaly","2_thermal", true(), null())
| where isnotnull(stage)
| transaction host maxspan=2h startswith=eval(stage="1_update") endswith=eval(stage="2_thermal")
| table _time, host, eventcount
tuning_guidance: Expect some benign post-update recalibration events; escalate only when paired with FW-005/FW-006 untrusted-source indicators.
investigation_steps: Correlate with FW-005/FW-006.
Validate the firmware image against HPE-published checksums if untrusted-source indicators are present.
response_guidance: Low independent urgency; escalate if correlated with other firmware-integrity indicators.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: IML SmartArray/Storage Controller Fault Following Privileged Login
description: An IML storage-controller fault or predictive-failure entry occurs shortly after a privileged iLO login, which given the OOB path's ability to reconfigure or wipe RAID arrays directly, is treated as a potential precursor to or corroboration of a destructive storage attack.

data_sources.name: IML + iLO Security Log
data_sources.path: IML storage-fault entries joined with login events
data_sources.description: Sequence of privileged login followed by storage-controller fault.

detection_logic: Sequences a successful privileged login with a subsequent storage-controller fault/predictive-failure IML entry within a bounded window.
spl:
index=ilo (sourcetype=ilo_iml event="StorageControllerFault") OR (sourcetype=ilo_security event="Login" result="Success" privilege="Administrator")
| eval stage=case(event="Login","1_login", event="StorageControllerFault","2_fault", true(), null())
| where isnotnull(stage)
| transaction host maxspan=30m startswith=eval(stage="1_login") endswith=eval(stage="2_fault")
| table _time, host, user, eventcount
tuning_guidance: Correlate with known maintenance windows for storage-firmware or RAID-configuration work.
investigation_steps: Determine whether a RAID configuration change (ILO storage config) or firmware update accompanied the fault.
Treat as a live incident if unconfirmed on a production host.
response_guidance: Escalate immediately if unconfirmed; verify data integrity/backups for the affected host.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: IML Records Excessive Correctable Memory Errors (Rowhammer-Adjacent Pattern)
description: A high volume of correctable memory errors is logged against the same DIMM/rank in a short window. Almost always benign hardware degradation, but included as a defense-in-depth indicator since sustained memory-fault-inducing techniques could theoretically manifest similarly; primarily useful for hardware reliability rather than security.

data_sources.name: IML
data_sources.description: Correctable memory error entries.

detection_logic: Counts correctable memory error entries per host/component in a rolling window.
spl:
index=ilo sourcetype=ilo_iml event="CorrectableMemoryError"
| bin _time span=1h
| stats count as error_count by host, component, _time
| where error_count>=50
tuning_guidance: Primarily a hardware-reliability signal; route to hardware operations, not the security queue, by default.
investigation_steps: Standard hardware fault-isolation procedure.
response_guidance: Replace/reseat the affected DIMM per standard hardware procedure.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1499: Endpoint Denial of Service

author: Threat Detection Library

title: IML Forwarding to SIEM Stopped While Local IML Continues to Grow
description: The device continues to generate new local IML entries (confirmed via direct polling or a subsequent forwarding resumption) while no corresponding entries arrived at the SIEM for an extended period, indicating the forwarding pipeline for this specific log type was disrupted independent of the device's own operation — consistent with ILO-033/ILO-034 but scoped to IML rather than the general Security Log.

data_sources.name: IML + SIEM ingestion metadata
data_sources.path: IML entry count comparison, local vs. forwarded
data_sources.description: Detects a forwarding gap independent of a specific configuration-change event.

detection_logic: Compares local IML entry counts (via periodic direct poll) against SIEM-ingested IML entry counts for the same window and flags a material mismatch.
spl:
| tstats count as forwarded_count where index=ilo sourcetype=ilo_iml by host
| join type=left host [ | inputlookup ilo_direct_poll_iml_counts.csv ]
| eval gap=local_count-forwarded_count
| where gap > 10
| table host, local_count, forwarded_count, gap
tuning_guidance: Requires a periodic direct-poll mechanism outside the normal forwarding pipeline to serve as ground truth.
investigation_steps: Verify network path between the device and the SIEM/collector.
Check for ILO-033/ILO-034 configuration-change events as the likely cause.
response_guidance: Restore forwarding and treat an unexplained gap as a probable anti-forensics attempt.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: AHS Data Collection Disabled
description: Active Health System data collection was disabled on the device, which removes a rich forensic/telemetry source used by HPE support and, when correlated, by security investigations reconstructing detailed hardware/firmware state history.

data_sources.name: iLO Security Log
data_sources.description: AHS enablement state-change events.

detection_logic: Filters configuration change events disabling AHS data collection.
spl:
index=ilo sourcetype=ilo_security event="AhsStateChanged" new_state="Disabled"
| table _time, host, user, src_ip
tuning_guidance: Low volume; alert on all occurrences.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification.
response_guidance: Re-enable if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: AHS Log Downloaded (Bulk Diagnostic Export)
description: An AHS diagnostic log bundle was downloaded via iLO. AHS bundles contain detailed hardware/firmware/config history and, while a routine HPE-support workflow, could also be used by an insider or attacker to exfiltrate detailed device configuration for reconnaissance of a broader attack.

data_sources.name: iLO Security Log
data_sources.description: AHS log download events.

detection_logic: Filters AHS log download events.
spl:
index=ilo sourcetype=ilo_security event="AhsLogDownloaded"
| table _time, host, user, src_ip
tuning_guidance: Expected during support engagements; correlate against open HPE support case numbers where available.
investigation_steps: Confirm against an active support case if unfamiliar.
response_guidance: Low urgency alone; escalate if the account is otherwise suspicious.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1005: Data from Local System

author: Threat Detection Library

title: AHS Bulk Log Download Across Multiple Fleet Devices
description: The same account downloads AHS logs from an unusually large number of distinct devices in a short window, which is atypical for a routine single-device support case and more consistent with bulk reconnaissance or exfiltration of fleet-wide configuration detail.

data_sources.name: iLO Security Log (fleet-aggregated)
data_sources.path: AHS log download events, aggregated across devices
data_sources.description: Distinct-device count per account in a rolling window.

detection_logic: Counts distinct devices with an AHS download by the same account in a rolling window.
spl:
index=ilo sourcetype=ilo_security event="AhsLogDownloaded"
| bin _time span=1h
| stats dc(host) as distinct_devices by user, _time
| where distinct_devices>=10
tuning_guidance: Tune out known fleet-health-monitoring automation accounts.
investigation_steps: Identify the account and confirm against known fleet-support tooling.
response_guidance: Investigate if not attributable to approved tooling.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1005: Data from Local System

author: Threat Detection Library

title: AHS Retention/Rotation Setting Reduced
description: The AHS data retention window was reduced, shortening how far back diagnostic/forensic history is available should an investigation later require it.

data_sources.name: iLO Security Log
data_sources.description: AHS retention setting-change events.

detection_logic: Filters AHS retention configuration change events where the new value is lower than the previous value.
spl:
index=ilo sourcetype=ilo_security event="AhsRetentionChanged"
| where new_retention < old_retention
| table _time, host, user, old_retention, new_retention
tuning_guidance: Low volume; alert on all occurrences.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification.
response_guidance: Revert if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: AHS Reports Unexpected Configuration Drift From Known-Good Baseline
description: AHS-reported hardware/firmware configuration state for a device diverges from its last known-good baseline snapshot outside of a tracked change window, which can surface configuration drift missed by event-based detections (e.g. due to a forwarding gap) via a secondary, independent data source.

data_sources.name: AHS export
data_sources.description: Periodic configuration snapshot compared against a stored baseline.

detection_logic: Compares a periodic AHS-derived configuration hash/snapshot against the last approved baseline and flags drift outside a tracked change window.
spl:
| inputlookup ahs_config_snapshots.csv
| join type=left host [ | inputlookup ahs_config_baseline.csv ]
| where config_hash!=baseline_hash
| lookup change_tickets.csv host OUTPUT ticket_id
| where isnull(ticket_id)
| table host, config_hash, baseline_hash
tuning_guidance: Requires a maintained baseline snapshot and change-ticket process; positioned as a backstop for gaps in event-based detection rather than a primary control.
investigation_steps: Identify the specific configuration items that drifted.
Cross-reference against event-based detections (FW-###, ILO-021/022, ILO-024-032) for the same window.
response_guidance: Investigate any unticketed drift; treat as a potential missed event if no corresponding configuration-change alert fired.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1543: Create or Modify System Process

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Intelligent Provisioning Launched on Production Host
description: Intelligent Provisioning (HPE's embedded OS-deployment/recovery environment) was launched via iLO on a host tagged as production. IP provides low-level access to storage configuration, OS deployment, and firmware update tooling, so use on an in-service host is high-value to investigate.

data_sources.name: iLO Security Log
data_sources.description: Intelligent Provisioning launch events cross-referenced with an asset-criticality lookup.

detection_logic: Filters Intelligent Provisioning launch events joined against a production-tagging lookup.
spl:
index=ilo sourcetype=ilo_security event="IntelligentProvisioningLaunched"
| lookup asset_criticality.csv host OUTPUT tier
| where tier="production"
| table _time, host, user, src_ip
tuning_guidance: Expected during planned reprovisioning/recovery; require a change ticket for production hosts.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification immediately.
Check for a concurrent Virtual Media mount or boot override.
response_guidance: Treat as a live incident if unconfirmed on a production host; the host's storage/OS may be about to be reimaged.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Intelligent Provisioning Used to Modify Storage/RAID Configuration
description: Intelligent Provisioning's Smart Storage Administrator function was used to modify RAID/array configuration on an in-service host, which can result in data loss and is a documented destructive technique against server hardware via the OOB management path.

data_sources.name: iLO Security Log
data_sources.description: Storage configuration change events originating from Intelligent Provisioning.

detection_logic: Filters storage configuration change events with source context indicating Intelligent Provisioning.
spl:
index=ilo sourcetype=ilo_security event="StorageConfigChanged" source_context="IntelligentProvisioning"
| table _time, host, user, action
tuning_guidance: Very low expected volume outside planned rebuild/reprovisioning; alert on all occurrences on production hosts.
investigation_steps: Treat as a live incident.
Verify backups exist and are current before any further action on the host.
response_guidance: Halt any pending destructive operation immediately if unconfirmed.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Intelligent Provisioning Firmware Update Path Used Outside Standard Channel
description: A firmware update was applied via Intelligent Provisioning's local update path rather than the standard Redfish/iLO-driven Service Pack for ProLiant (SPP) channel, which is a less commonly audited path and worth correlating with FW-005/FW-006 downgrade/untrusted-source indicators.

data_sources.name: iLO Security Log
data_sources.description: Firmware update events with source context indicating Intelligent Provisioning.

detection_logic: Filters firmware update events with source context indicating Intelligent Provisioning.
spl:
index=ilo sourcetype=ilo_security event="FirmwareUpdate" source_context="IntelligentProvisioning"
| table _time, host, user, component
tuning_guidance: Expected during initial provisioning/imaging workflows; correlate with FW-005/FW-006 for the remainder.
investigation_steps: Cross-reference with FW-005/FW-006.
response_guidance: Same as FW-005/FW-006 depending on findings.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: iLO-Initiated Logical Drive Deletion
description: A logical drive/array was deleted via the iLO-accessible Smart Storage Administrator interface, which is destructive and, combined with OOB access bypassing the OS entirely, represents one of the most severe possible outcomes of iLO compromise.

data_sources.name: iLO Security Log
data_sources.description: Logical drive deletion events.

detection_logic: Filters logical drive deletion events.
spl:
index=ilo sourcetype=ilo_security event="LogicalDriveDeleted"
| table _time, host, user, logical_drive, src_ip
tuning_guidance: Alert on every occurrence; there is essentially never a routine reason for this on an in-service host outside a confirmed decommission ticket.
investigation_steps: Treat as a live incident immediately.
Verify backup status for the affected host.
Identify and disable the acting account.
response_guidance: This is a destructive event already in progress or completed; engage incident response and data-recovery procedures immediately.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: iLO Login From Outside the Declared OOB Management Network
description: An iLO login originated from a source IP outside the declared out-of-band management network/VLAN, indicating either a network segmentation gap or that the iLO interface is reachable from a broader network than intended — referenced by ILO-006 as the segmentation-aware companion detection.

data_sources.name: iLO Security Log
data_sources.description: Login events cross-referenced against the declared OOB CIDR range.

detection_logic: Filters login events where src_ip falls outside the declared OOB management CIDR ranges.
spl:
index=ilo sourcetype=ilo_security event="Login" result="Success"
| where NOT cidrmatch("10.250.0.0/16", src_ip)
| table _time, host, user, src_ip
tuning_guidance: Requires maintaining the OOB CIDR range(s) accurately; treat any hit as a segmentation finding regardless of the specific login's legitimacy.
investigation_steps: Determine whether this reflects a segmentation gap or unauthorized network exposure.
Investigate the specific login per ILO-001 through ILO-009.
response_guidance: Remediate the segmentation gap; investigate the specific access per standard authentication-detection response.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: iLO Configuration Exported
description: The full iLO configuration (which can include network, user, and security settings) was exported. Legitimate for backup/migration, but a bulk configuration export is also a reconnaissance step of interest, and the exported file may itself require careful handling if it contains sensitive settings.

data_sources.name: iLO Security Log
data_sources.description: Configuration export events.

detection_logic: Filters configuration export events.
spl:
index=ilo sourcetype=ilo_security event="ConfigurationExported"
| table _time, host, user, src_ip
tuning_guidance: Expected during planned backup/migration; tune out known automation accounts and alert on the remainder.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification.
response_guidance: Low urgency alone; escalate if paired with other suspicious indicators or a fleet-wide pattern (ILO-043).

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1005: Data from Local System

author: Threat Detection Library

title: iLO Configuration Imported
description: A configuration file was imported into iLO, potentially making a broad set of changes (network, users, security settings) in a single operation. Because a single import can silently make many changes at once, it warrants a higher scrutiny bar than any single equivalent manual change.

data_sources.name: iLO Security Log
data_sources.description: Configuration import events.

detection_logic: Filters configuration import events.
spl:
index=ilo sourcetype=ilo_security event="ConfigurationImported"
| table _time, host, user, src_ip
tuning_guidance: Expected during planned provisioning/fleet-standardization; require a change ticket for imports against already-in-service hosts.
investigation_steps: Diff the resulting configuration against the pre-import baseline to identify exactly what changed.
Confirm business justification.
response_guidance: Revert to the pre-import configuration if unauthorized and audit every setting the import touched.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: iLO Reset to Factory Default
description: iLO was reset to factory default settings, which wipes all custom configuration including users, network settings, certificates, and — critically — local audit-relevant configuration state, making it both a disruptive and a strong anti-forensics event.

data_sources.name: iLO Security Log
data_sources.description: Factory-reset events, typically captured just before local log state is wiped.

detection_logic: Filters factory-reset events; because forwarding may itself be reset by this action, this detection should be treated as a low-reliability last line of defense behind ILO-035's heartbeat-gap detection.
spl:
index=ilo sourcetype=ilo_security event="FactoryReset"
| table _time, host, user, src_ip
tuning_guidance: Alert on all occurrences; exception-list only via a confirmed decommission/re-provisioning change ticket.
investigation_steps: Treat as a live incident.
Immediately capture any remaining forwarded logs for the device before the gap becomes unrecoverable.
Physically or out-of-band verify the device's post-reset state.
response_guidance: Treat the device as compromised and requiring full re-provisioning under controlled conditions, including credential and certificate reissuance.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: iLO License Key Changed/Removed
description: The iLO license key was changed or removed, which can downgrade available functionality (including some security features that are license-gated on certain iLO tiers) without any other visible configuration change.

data_sources.name: iLO Security Log
data_sources.description: License key change events.

detection_logic: Filters license key change/removal events.
spl:
index=ilo sourcetype=ilo_security event="LicenseChanged"
| table _time, host, user, action
tuning_guidance: Low volume; alert on all occurrences.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification.
Verify no security-relevant licensed feature was disabled as a side effect.
response_guidance: Restore the correct license if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: iLO UID (Unit Identification) LED Activated Outside Change Window
description: The chassis UID LED was activated via iLO outside a declared change/maintenance window. Legitimately used by data-center technicians to physically locate a server before service; unexpected activation can indicate an attacker (or an unauthorized insider) preparing to physically locate and access the hardware.

data_sources.name: iLO Security Log
data_sources.description: UID LED activation events cross-referenced against a maintenance calendar.

detection_logic: Filters UID LED activation events where a maintenance-window lookup does not cover the event time.
spl:
index=ilo sourcetype=ilo_security event="UidLedChanged" new_state="On"
| lookup maintenance_windows.csv host, _time OUTPUT in_window
| where isnull(in_window) OR in_window=0
| table _time, host, user
tuning_guidance: High false-positive rate without a maintained maintenance-window lookup; low individual severity in any case.
investigation_steps: Confirm with data-center operations whether physical access was authorized.
response_guidance: Low urgency; primarily useful as a supporting signal alongside FW-004 physical-tamper indicators.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1592: Gather Victim Host Information

author: Threat Detection Library

title: HPE Compute Ops Management: Device Claimed Into a New Workspace
description: A device managed via HPE Compute Ops Management (COM, the cloud-based fleet management service) was claimed into a different COM workspace/tenant than its expected home, which could reflect legitimate reorganization or an attempt to move management control of the device to an attacker-controlled tenant.

data_sources.name: iLO Security Log
data_sources.description: COM workspace claim/unclaim events.

detection_logic: Filters COM claim events where the workspace_id differs from the device's expected workspace per an asset inventory lookup.
spl:
index=ilo sourcetype=ilo_security event="ComWorkspaceClaimed"
| lookup asset_inventory.csv host OUTPUT expected_workspace_id
| where workspace_id!=expected_workspace_id
| table _time, host, user, workspace_id, expected_workspace_id
tuning_guidance: Low volume; alert on all occurrences outside planned fleet reorganization.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification for the workspace change.
Verify the destination workspace is legitimately owned by the organization.
response_guidance: Unclaim and reclaim into the correct workspace if unauthorized; treat as a fleet-management-plane compromise indicator.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: HPE Compute Ops Management: Remote Firmware/Server Profile Update Pushed Fleet-Wide
description: A firmware update or server profile change was pushed from HPE Compute Ops Management to an unusually large number of devices at once, consistent with either a legitimate scheduled fleet update or a compromised COM tenant/account being used to push malicious changes at scale.

data_sources.name: iLO Security Log (fleet-aggregated)
data_sources.path: iLO Security Log, aggregated across devices
data_sources.description: COM-originated firmware/profile push events.

detection_logic: Counts distinct devices receiving a COM-originated firmware/profile push from the same operation ID in a rolling window.
spl:
index=ilo sourcetype=ilo_security event="FirmwareUpdate" source_context="ComRemote"
| bin _time span=1h
| stats dc(host) as distinct_devices, values(component) as components by user, _time
| where distinct_devices>=15
tuning_guidance: Baseline the organization's normal COM-driven fleet-update scope; scheduled maintenance windows will legitimately trigger this.
investigation_steps: Confirm against a change ticket for planned fleet-wide firmware deployment.
Cross-reference against FW-005/FW-006 for downgrade or untrusted-source indicators.
response_guidance: If unauthorized, treat as a fleet-wide incident originating from the COM tenant; suspend the COM account/API token and audit all recent COM activity.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Fleet-Wide Spike in Failed iLO Authentication Across Distinct Devices
description: A large number of distinct iLO-managed devices report authentication failures within a short window, which given how tightly OOB access is normally scoped, is a strong indicator of an automated fleet-wide credential attack (e.g. a leaked shared local-admin password being tried across the entire fleet).

data_sources.name: iLO Security Log (fleet-aggregated)
data_sources.path: iLO Security Log, aggregated across devices
data_sources.description: Distinct-device failure count in a rolling window.

detection_logic: Counts distinct hosts with at least one authentication failure from a given source in a rolling window.
spl:
index=ilo sourcetype=ilo_security event="Login" result="Failed"
| bin _time span=15m
| stats dc(host) as distinct_hosts by src_ip, _time
| where distinct_hosts>=10
tuning_guidance: Very low expected false-positive rate; a single legitimate account rarely fails auth across many distinct devices in a short window.
investigation_steps: Identify the source IP and block at the OOB network boundary immediately.
Determine whether any of the attempted credentials succeeded elsewhere in the fleet.
response_guidance: Treat as an active fleet-wide credential attack; rotate the shared local-admin credential across the fleet if one is in use.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Fleet-Wide Identical Configuration Change Applied Outside Fleet-Management Tooling
description: The same specific configuration change (e.g. the same setting to the same new value) is applied across many distinct devices by individual iLO sessions rather than via COM/OneView fleet tooling, suggesting a scripted attack iterating credentials or a compromised automation account operating outside its normal orchestration path.

data_sources.name: iLO Security Log (fleet-aggregated)
data_sources.path: iLO Security Log, aggregated across devices
data_sources.description: Identical setting/value change events across many hosts, outside COM/OneView source context.

detection_logic: Groups configuration change events by setting/new_value and counts distinct hosts, excluding events with COM/OneView source context.
spl:
index=ilo sourcetype=ilo_security event="SecuritySettingChanged" NOT source_context IN ("ComRemote", "OneView")
| bin _time span=1h
| stats dc(host) as distinct_devices by setting, new_value, user, _time
| where distinct_devices>=10
tuning_guidance: Tune out known non-COM/OneView bulk-configuration scripts used by the platform team, ideally by migrating them to a recognized source_context instead.
investigation_steps: Identify the account/token performing the change and confirm it is not a compromised automation credential.
Enumerate all affected devices.
response_guidance: Treat as a fleet-wide incident if unconfirmed; suspend the acting account/token pending review.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: HPE OneView New Administrator Account Created
description: A new administrator-level account was created in HPE OneView. Because OneView can manage server profiles, firmware baselines, and network configuration across the entire managed fleet, a new admin account here is a direct path to fleet-wide compromise via the OneView-driven fleet-change chain.

data_sources.name: OneView Audit Log
data_sources.description: User account creation events with role assignment.

detection_logic: Filters OneView audit events for new user creation with an administrator role.
spl:
index=oneview sourcetype=oneview_audit event="UserCreated" role="Infrastructure administrator"
| table _time, user, created_by, role
tuning_guidance: Very low expected volume; alert on all occurrences.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification with the requesting manager.
Verify against a change ticket.
response_guidance: Disable the account immediately if unconfirmed and audit every action it has taken.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: HPE OneView Server Profile Applied to Unexpected Number of Servers
description: A single server-profile apply/update operation in OneView targets an unusually large number of managed servers at once. OneView server profiles can carry firmware baselines, boot order, network, and BIOS settings, so a large-scale apply is a high-leverage fleet-wide attack vector if driven by a compromised OneView account.

data_sources.name: OneView Audit Log
data_sources.description: Server profile apply/update events with target counts.

detection_logic: Filters server profile apply events where the target device count exceeds a fleet-scale threshold.
spl:
index=oneview sourcetype=oneview_audit event="ServerProfileApplied"
| where target_count>=15
| table _time, user, profile_name, target_count
tuning_guidance: Baseline the organization's normal fleet-standardization batch size; scheduled rollouts will legitimately trigger this.
investigation_steps: Confirm against a change ticket for planned fleet-wide profile rollout.
Review the specific profile contents for unexpected settings.
response_guidance: If unauthorized, treat as a fleet-wide incident: identify every targeted server and roll back the profile.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: HPE OneView Firmware Baseline Downgraded
description: A OneView firmware baseline (the reference firmware bundle applied fleet-wide to managed servers) was changed to a lower version than previously configured, which — because OneView will then push the downgrade to every server assigned that baseline — is a fleet-scale version of FW-005 with a substantially larger blast radius.

data_sources.name: OneView Audit Log
data_sources.description: Firmware baseline change events with before/after version.

detection_logic: Compares old_version and new_version on firmware baseline change events and flags any decrease.
spl:
index=oneview sourcetype=oneview_audit event="FirmwareBaselineChanged"
| eval downgrade=if(old_version>new_version, 1, 0)
| where downgrade=1
| table _time, user, baseline_name, old_version, new_version
tuning_guidance: Alert on every confirmed downgrade; treat with the same urgency as FW-005 given the larger blast radius.
investigation_steps: Identify every server profile/group referencing the affected baseline.
Confirm business justification (rare: recovery from a bad firmware release).
response_guidance: Revert the baseline immediately and audit all servers that received the downgraded firmware before this was caught.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: HPE OneView Managed Appliance/Device Removed From Management
description: A device was removed from HPE OneView management, which stops OneView-driven monitoring/compliance checks for that device and can be used to quietly take a device out of centralized visibility ahead of unauthorized direct access.

data_sources.name: OneView Audit Log
data_sources.description: Device removal events.

detection_logic: Filters device removal events.
spl:
index=oneview sourcetype=oneview_audit event="DeviceRemoved"
| table _time, user, host
tuning_guidance: Expected during planned decommissioning; require a change ticket for removal of in-service devices.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification.
Check for subsequent direct (non-OneView-mediated) iLO access to the device.
response_guidance: Re-add to management if unauthorized and monitor the device closely for direct access.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: HPE OneView Audit Logging Disabled or Retention Reduced
description: OneView's own audit logging was disabled, or its retention window was reduced, which given OneView's fleet-wide reach, is a high-impact anti-forensics action that can obscure a broad range of subsequent fleet-management-plane abuse.

data_sources.name: OneView Audit Log
data_sources.description: Audit configuration change events.

detection_logic: Filters audit configuration change events indicating logging disablement or retention reduction.
spl:
index=oneview sourcetype=oneview_audit event="AuditConfigChanged" (setting="LoggingEnabled" new_value="false" OR setting="RetentionDays")
| table _time, user, setting, new_value
tuning_guidance: Alert on all occurrences; essentially no routine reason to reduce OneView's own audit posture.
investigation_steps: Treat as a live incident.
Immediately export current OneView audit data before further tampering can occur.
response_guidance: Restore full audit logging immediately and treat the OneView tenant as potentially compromised pending investigation.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: HPE OneView SSO/Directory Trust Configuration Changed
description: OneView's SSO or directory-trust configuration (which governs how identity federation grants access to the fleet-management console) was changed, potentially allowing an attacker-controlled identity provider or group to gain OneView access.

data_sources.name: OneView Audit Log
data_sources.description: SSO/directory trust configuration change events.

detection_logic: Filters SSO/directory trust configuration change events.
spl:
index=oneview sourcetype=oneview_audit event="SsoConfigChanged"
| table _time, user, setting, new_value
tuning_guidance: Very low expected volume; alert on all occurrences.
investigation_steps: Verify the new configuration against the organization's approved identity provider.
response_guidance: Revert if unauthorized and audit any logins that occurred under the new trust configuration.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1484: Domain or Tenant Policy Modification

author: Threat Detection Library

title: HPE OneView Network/Uplink Configuration Changed Across Multiple Enclosures
description: A network or uplink-set configuration change is applied across multiple OneView-managed enclosures/interconnects in a short window, which can disrupt connectivity fleet-wide and is a plausible mechanism for a management-plane-driven denial-of-service attack.

data_sources.name: OneView Audit Log
data_sources.description: Network/uplink configuration change events across enclosures.

detection_logic: Counts distinct enclosures with a network/uplink configuration change by the same account in a rolling window.
spl:
index=oneview sourcetype=oneview_audit event="NetworkConfigChanged"
| bin _time span=1h
| stats dc(enclosure) as distinct_enclosures by user, _time
| where distinct_enclosures>=3
tuning_guidance: Expected during planned network maintenance; require a change ticket for multi-enclosure network changes.
investigation_steps: Confirm against a change ticket.
Assess current connectivity impact across affected enclosures immediately.
response_guidance: Revert if unauthorized; treat as an active availability incident given the fleet-wide blast radius.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1498: Network Denial of Service

author: Threat Detection Library

title: HPE OneView API Token Issued With Broad Scope
description: A OneView API session/token was issued with broad administrative scope for a non-interactive/automation context, expanding the potential impact if that token is later leaked or misused.

data_sources.name: OneView Audit Log
data_sources.description: API token/session issuance events with scope.

detection_logic: Filters token issuance events where scope is administrative and the requesting context is non-interactive.
spl:
index=oneview sourcetype=oneview_audit event="ApiTokenIssued" scope="Infrastructure administrator" client_type="NonInteractive"
| table _time, user, scope, client_id
tuning_guidance: Review against the principle of least privilege; automation accounts should generally hold scoped, not full-administrator, tokens.
investigation_steps: Confirm the automation use case actually requires administrative scope.
response_guidance: Reissue with reduced scope if not justified.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: iLO Compromise Leading to OS-Level Bypass (Virtual Media / Boot Override Chain)
description: The flagship iLO attack chain: a successful login (especially one following repeated failures, ILO-004) is followed by a Virtual Media mount, a one-time boot override to that media, and a reboot — the complete sequence by which an attacker with only iLO access boots a host into fully attacker-controlled media, bypassing the installed OS and every one of its controls entirely. This correlation search ties together the individual VMEDIA-003/RC-004/ILO-021 detections into a single incident-level view.

data_sources.name: iLO Security Log
data_sources.description: Login, virtual media, boot override, and power/reboot events for the same host.

detection_logic: Sequences login success, virtual media attach, boot override, and reboot events for the same host within a bounded window.
spl:
index=ilo sourcetype=ilo_security (event="Login" result="Success") OR event="VirtualMediaAttached" OR event="OneTimeBootOverrideSet" OR (event="VirtualPowerControl" power_action="Reset")
| eval stage=case(event="Login","1_login", event="VirtualMediaAttached","2_media", event="OneTimeBootOverrideSet","3_boot", event="VirtualPowerControl","4_reboot", true(), null())
| where isnotnull(stage)
| transaction host maxspan=30m startswith=eval(stage="1_login")
| where mvcount(mvdedup(stage))>=4
| table _time, host, user, eventcount
tuning_guidance: Treat every confirmed instance of the full sequence as an incident; the individual component detections (VMEDIA-003, ILO-021) should already have alerted, so this search primarily serves incident consolidation and case escalation.
investigation_steps: Assume the host OS is compromised.
Identify the acting account and every action taken during the session.
Determine the source and content of the mounted media if possible.
response_guidance: Power off the host immediately, preserve the OOB session logs and mounted-media metadata, and treat the host as requiring full forensic imaging and rebuild.
author: Threat Detection Library

threshold.baseline_condition: login -> virtual media mount -> boot override -> reboot, same host

title: iLO Compromise Leading to Hypervisor-Level Compromise
description: A suspicious iLO Remote Console or Virtual Media session on a hypervisor host (e.g. ESXi, per this repository's own ESXi catalogue) is followed, within a short window, by suspicious activity observed in that hypervisor's own logs (e.g. new local account creation, SSH enablement, lockdown-mode disablement). Because iLO provides console access below the hypervisor layer, this chain represents an OOB-to-hypervisor pivot that hypervisor-native logging alone would attribute only to a local console session with no external context.

data_sources.name: iLO Security Log + Hypervisor Log
data_sources.path: iLO Remote Console/Virtual Media events joined with hypervisor management-plane events for the same host
data_sources.description: Cross-source correlation requiring both telemetry streams.

detection_logic: Sequences an iLO Remote Console/Virtual Media event with a subsequent hypervisor-management-plane change event on the same physical host within a bounded window.
spl:
(index=ilo sourcetype=ilo_security (event="RemoteConsoleSessionStarted" OR event="VirtualMediaAttached"))
OR (index=esxi (event="AccountCreated" OR event="SSHEnabled" OR event="LockdownModeDisabled"))
| eval stage=case(event="RemoteConsoleSessionStarted" OR event="VirtualMediaAttached","1_ilo", true(),"2_hypervisor")
| transaction host maxspan=1h startswith=eval(stage="1_ilo") endswith=eval(stage="2_hypervisor")
| table _time, host, eventcount
tuning_guidance: Requires a mapping between iLO-managed host identifiers and the hypervisor instance running on that physical host.
investigation_steps: Correlate the iLO session's acting account with the hypervisor-level change.
Review this repository's ESXi detection library for the specific hypervisor-side finding.
response_guidance: Treat as a live incident spanning both the management plane and the hypervisor; isolate the host and begin hypervisor-level forensic review.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Identity Compromise Leading to iLO Directory-Based Access
description: A directory/identity-provider account is observed being added to (or having permissions elevated within) an iLO-integrated directory group (ILO-015) shortly after that same account showed signs of compromise in the identity provider's own logs (e.g. impossible travel, a new MFA device registration, or a password reset outside self-service norms). This chain reflects an attacker pivoting from a compromised centralized identity directly into out-of-band hardware management scope.

data_sources.name: iLO Security Log + Identity Provider Log
data_sources.path: iLO directory group membership events joined with identity-provider account-risk events for the same account
data_sources.description: Cross-source correlation requiring both telemetry streams.

detection_logic: Sequences an identity-provider account-risk/compromise indicator with a subsequent iLO directory-group-membership grant for the same account within a bounded window.
spl:
(index=idp (event="ImpossibleTravel" OR event="NewMfaDeviceRegistered" OR event="PasswordResetOutOfBand"))
OR (index=ilo sourcetype=ilo_security event="DirectoryGroupIloAccessGranted")
| eval stage=case(event="DirectoryGroupIloAccessGranted","2_ilo_grant", true(),"1_idp_risk")
| transaction user maxspan=24h startswith=eval(stage="1_idp_risk") endswith=eval(stage="2_ilo_grant")
| table _time, user, eventcount
tuning_guidance: Requires identity-provider risk-signal ingestion in addition to iLO telemetry; high-value once available given the severity of the resulting access.
investigation_steps: Treat the identity compromise as confirmed pending investigation.
Immediately review what iLO-managed devices are reachable via the granted directory group.
response_guidance: Suspend the account across both the identity provider and iLO directory-group membership immediately; treat every device reachable via the group as potentially exposed.
author: Threat Detection Library

threshold.baseline_condition: identity-provider risk signal -> iLO directory-group access grant, same account

title: iLO Compromise Followed by Coordinated Anti-Forensics Across Log Sources
description: Multiple anti-forensics indicators (syslog redirection/disablement, IML/log clearing, factory reset, OneView audit-log disablement) occur against the same host or account within a short window, which taken together constitute much stronger evidence of a deliberate cover-up than any single event alone.

data_sources.name: iLO Security Log + IML + OneView Audit
data_sources.path: Anti-forensics event types across all iLO-related sources for the same host/account
data_sources.description: Correlation of ILO-033/034/036/044 and ONEVIEW-005 style events.

detection_logic: Counts distinct anti-forensics event types (syslog change, log clear, factory reset, OneView audit disable) for the same host/account in a rolling window.
spl:
index=ilo OR index=oneview (event="SyslogDestinationChanged" OR event="SyslogForwardingDisabled" OR event="LogCleared" OR event="FactoryReset" OR event="AuditConfigChanged")
| stats dc(event) as distinct_af_events, values(event) as events by host, user
| where distinct_af_events>=2
tuning_guidance: Very low expected false-positive rate; two or more distinct anti-forensics event types together should always be escalated.
investigation_steps: Treat as a confirmed active incident.
Immediately preserve any remaining forwarded logs across all sources.
Assume every subsequent action by the account is untrustworthy until proven otherwise.
response_guidance: Full incident response: isolate affected hosts, suspend the account across all platforms, and engage forensic imaging before further changes occur.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: iLO Destructive Attack Chain (Privileged Login → Storage Deletion → Power Cycle → Boot Failure)
description: The complete destructive-attack sequence named explicitly in this library's specification: a privileged iLO login is followed by a logical drive deletion (ILO-040), then a power cycle, and finally the host fails to boot (or boots into a recovery/empty state) — end-to-end evidence of an attacker (or catastrophically severe insider error) using OOB access to destroy data and force an outage.

data_sources.name: iLO Security Log + IML
data_sources.path: Login, storage deletion, power control, and subsequent boot-failure/no-OS IML events for the same host
data_sources.description: Full destructive-chain correlation.

detection_logic: Sequences login success, logical drive deletion, power control, and a subsequent boot-failure indicator for the same host within a bounded window.
spl:
index=ilo (sourcetype=ilo_security (event="Login" result="Success" privilege="Administrator") OR event="LogicalDriveDeleted" OR event="VirtualPowerControl") OR (sourcetype=ilo_iml event="BootFailure")
| eval stage=case(event="Login","1_login", event="LogicalDriveDeleted","2_delete", event="VirtualPowerControl","3_power", event="BootFailure","4_boot_fail", true(), null())
| where isnotnull(stage)
| transaction host maxspan=1h startswith=eval(stage="1_login")
| where mvcount(mvdedup(stage))>=3
| table _time, host, user, eventcount
tuning_guidance: Treat any confirmed occurrence of three or more stages as a confirmed severe incident regardless of stated justification; the individual components (ILO-040) should already have paged the on-call team.
investigation_steps: This is a confirmed destructive incident — engage full incident response immediately.
Determine whether backups exist and are current for the affected host.
Identify and suspend the acting account across the entire fleet, not just this device.
response_guidance: Full incident response: data-recovery procedures, account suspension fleet-wide, and root-cause investigation into how the account obtained this level of access.
author: Threat Detection Library

threshold.baseline_condition: privileged login -> storage deletion -> power cycle -> [boot failure], same host

title: HPE OneView-Driven Fleet-Wide Compromise Chain
description: The fleet-management-platform compromise chain named explicitly in this library's specification: a new OneView administrator account (ONEVIEW-001) or a broadly-scoped API token (ONEVIEW-008) is followed, within a short window, by a fleet-wide server-profile push (ONEVIEW-002), firmware baseline downgrade (ONEVIEW-003), or multi-enclosure network change (ONEVIEW-007) — the complete path by which compromising a single fleet-management platform yields control over the entire managed server estate at once.

data_sources.name: OneView Audit Log
data_sources.path: New admin/token issuance followed by fleet-scale change events
data_sources.description: Correlation of ONEVIEW-001/008 with ONEVIEW-002/003/007.

detection_logic: Sequences a new-admin or broad-token-issuance event with a subsequent fleet-scale change event by the same account within a bounded window.
spl:
index=oneview sourcetype=oneview_audit (event="UserCreated" role="Infrastructure administrator") OR (event="ApiTokenIssued" scope="Infrastructure administrator") OR event="ServerProfileApplied" OR event="FirmwareBaselineChanged" OR event="NetworkConfigChanged"
| eval stage=case(event="UserCreated" OR event="ApiTokenIssued","1_grant", true(),"2_fleet_change")
| transaction user maxspan=2h startswith=eval(stage="1_grant") endswith=eval(stage="2_fleet_change")
| table _time, user, eventcount
tuning_guidance: Treat any confirmed occurrence as a fleet-wide incident; the individual component detections should already have alerted, so this search consolidates them into a single incident view.
investigation_steps: Enumerate every device targeted by the fleet-scale change.
Suspend the OneView account/token immediately.
Assess the OneView tenant itself for broader compromise (e.g. how the admin account/token was created).
response_guidance: Full incident response spanning the entire managed fleet: suspend the account, roll back the fleet-scale change everywhere it was applied, and audit the OneView tenant's own access controls.
author: Threat Detection Library

threshold.baseline_condition: new admin/broad token -> fleet-scale change, same account

title: iLO Out-of-Band Access Immediately Preceding OS-Level Privileged Account Creation
description: An iLO Remote Console or Virtual Media session on a host is followed, within a short window, by a new privileged local account being created on that host's operating system — consistent with an attacker using OOB console access to establish OS-level persistence directly, bypassing any network-based OS access controls entirely.

data_sources.name: iLO Security Log + OS Audit Log
data_sources.path: iLO console/media session events joined with OS-level account creation events for the same host
data_sources.description: Cross-source correlation requiring OS-level telemetry in addition to iLO.

detection_logic: Sequences an iLO Remote Console/Virtual Media session with a subsequent OS-level privileged account creation event on the same host within a bounded window.
spl:
(index=ilo sourcetype=ilo_security (event="RemoteConsoleSessionStarted" OR event="VirtualMediaAttached"))
OR (index=os_audit event="PrivilegedAccountCreated")
| eval stage=case(event="RemoteConsoleSessionStarted" OR event="VirtualMediaAttached","1_ilo", true(),"2_os_account")
| transaction host maxspan=1h startswith=eval(stage="1_ilo") endswith=eval(stage="2_os_account")
| table _time, host, eventcount
tuning_guidance: Requires OS-level audit ingestion mapped to the same host identifier used by iLO; exclude known imaging/provisioning workflows where a first-boot account is expected.
investigation_steps: Correlate the iLO session's acting account with the OS account creation.
Treat the new OS account as attacker-controlled pending investigation.
response_guidance: Disable the new OS account and treat the host's OS as requiring integrity verification.

title: Coordinated iLO Activity Across Multiple Out-of-Band Vendor Platforms
description: The same source IP or account pattern generates authentication or configuration-change activity against both HPE iLO and a different out-of-band management platform (e.g. Dell iDRAC, per this library's iDRAC catalogue) within a short window, consistent with an attacker running a single credential-stuffing or scripted-attack campaign against the entire heterogeneous OOB management estate rather than one vendor in isolation.

data_sources.name: iLO Security Log + iDRAC Log
data_sources.path: Authentication/configuration events from both OOB platforms correlated by source IP or account
data_sources.description: Requires ingesting both vendors' OOB management telemetry into the same search.

detection_logic: Counts distinct OOB management platforms (iLO, iDRAC) with authentication or configuration-change activity from the same source IP in a rolling window.
spl:
(index=ilo sourcetype=ilo_security (event="Login" OR event="*Changed")) OR (index=idrac sourcetype=idrac_security (event="Login" OR event="*Changed"))
| eval platform=if(index="ilo","iLO","iDRAC")
| bin _time span=1h
| stats dc(platform) as distinct_platforms, values(platform) as platforms by src_ip, _time
| where distinct_platforms>=2
tuning_guidance: Very low expected false-positive rate given how rarely a single legitimate operator/account routinely manages both vendor estates from the same source in a short window; excludes known cross-platform fleet-management tooling via source allowlist.
investigation_steps: Identify the source IP and determine whether it maps to known, approved cross-platform management tooling.
If not, treat as a coordinated campaign against the entire OOB estate.
response_guidance: Block the source at the OOB network boundary across both platforms and rotate any credentials that may have been targeted on either vendor's estate.
